knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The second subderivative of the indicator of \(C\) at \(\bar x\) relative to \(\bar v\) is
\[
d_e^2\delta_C(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w):=\liminf_{\substack{t\downarrow0\\w'\to w}}\frac{\delta_C(\bar x+tw')-\delta_C(\bar x)-t\langle\bar v,w'\rangle}{\tfrac12t^2}.
\]
Equivalently, only perturbations satisfying \(\bar x+tw'\in C\) contribute finite values. Thus the model records the second-order feasible approach geometry of \(C\) after subtracting the first-order normal term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The indicator’s second subderivative measures second-order feasible approaches after removing the linear contribution of the reference normal.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in C\), the limiting normal cone and indicator subdifferential satisfy
\[
N_C(x)=\partial\delta_C(x).
\]
Their graphs and graphical derivatives therefore satisfy
\[
\operatorname{gph}N_C=\operatorname{gph}\partial\delta_C
\]
and, for every \(w\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[
DN_C(\bar x,\bar v)(w)=D(\partial\delta_C)(\bar x,\bar v)(w)=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:(w,z)\in T_{\operatorname{gph}N_C}(\bar x,\bar v)\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal-cone mapping equals the indicator subdifferential, so their graphs and graphical derivatives coincide.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite-dimensional epi-to-proto correspondence under prox-regularity and subdifferential continuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional prox-regular epi-to-proto theorem with the \(t^2/2\) normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the stated assumptions, the difference-quotient mappings
\[
w\mapsto\frac{\partial f(\bar x+tw)-\bar v}{t}
\]
graphically converge as \(t\downarrow0\). Hence \(\partial f\) is proto-differentiable at \((\bar x,\bar v)\), and its proto-derivative is determined by the second epi-derivative:
\[
D(\partial f)(\bar x,\bar v)(w)=\partial\!\left(\frac12d_e^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)\right)(w)
\quad\text{for every }\(w\in\mathbb R^n\).
\]
The subdifferential on the right is taken with respect to the direction variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a twice epi-differentiable prox-regular function, the proto-derivative of its subgradient is the subgradient of half its second epi-derivative.
knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient Proto-Differentiability

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second Derivatives and Quadratic Expansions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes extended twice differentiability of differentiable prox-regular functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}} be differentiable at \bar x and prox-regular there for \bar v=\nabla f(\bar x). The following are equivalent: (a) f is twice differentiable at \bar x in the extended sense; (b) \partial f is differentiable at \bar x; (c) f has a quadratic expansion at \bar x. Whenever these conditions hold, \nabla^2f(\bar x) is symmetric and f is lower-\mathcal C^2 on a neighborhood of \bar x.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a differentiable function that is prox-regular at the point for its gradient, extended twice differentiability, differentiability of the subgradient mapping, and existence of a quadratic expansion are equivalent. The resulting Hessian is symmetric, and the function is locally lower-C2.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is prox-regular at }\bar x\text{ for }\bar v
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is extended twice differentiable at }\bar x\iff\partial f\text{ is differentiable at }\bar x\iff f\text{ has a quadratic expansion at }\bar x;\quad \nabla^2f(\bar x)=\nabla^2f(\bar x)^T,\quad f\text{ is locally lower-}\mathcal C^2.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proto-Differentiability and Twice Epi-Differentiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes proto-differentiability of prox-regular subgradient mappings and identifies their proto-derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}} is prox-regular at \bar x for \bar v\in\partial f(\bar x) and is subdifferentially continuous there. Then \partial f is proto-differentiable at \bar x for \bar v if and only if f is twice epi-differentiable at \bar x for \bar v. In that case h=\tfrac12d^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v) is proper and \[D(\partial f)(\bar x\mid\bar v)=\partial h.\] Without subdifferential continuity, the same conclusions hold after replacing \partial f by any sufficiently close f-attentive localization at (\bar x,\bar v).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a prox-regular and subdifferentially continuous function, proto-differentiability of the subgradient mapping is equivalent to twice epi-differentiability of the function, and the proto-derivative is the subdifferential of half the second epi-derivative. Without subdifferential continuity, this remains valid for sufficiently close attentive localizations.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is prox-regular at }\bar x\text{ for }\bar v
f\text{ is subdifferentially continuous at }\bar x\text{ for }\bar v\text{, unless an }f\text{-attentive localization is used}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial f\text{ is proto-differentiable at }(\bar x,\bar v)\iff f\text{ is twice epi-differentiable at }(\bar x,\bar v),\qquad D(\partial f)(\bar x\mid\bar v)=\partial[\tfrac12d^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Difference-Quotient Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates second-order difference quotients to subgradient, Moreau-envelope, and proximal-mapping difference quotients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}, let f(\bar x) be finite, and let \bar v\in\partial f(\bar x). For every \tau>0, \[\partial\!\left[\tfrac12\Delta_\tau^2 f(\bar x\mid\bar v)\right]=[\Delta_\tau\partial f](\bar x\mid\bar v).\] If additionally \bar x=0, \bar v=0, and f(0)=0=\min f, then for every \tau>0 and \lambda>0, \[e_\lambda\!\left[\tfrac12\Delta_\tau^2f(0\mid0)\right]=\left[\tfrac12\Delta_\tau^2(e_\lambda f)\right](0\mid0),\qquad P_\lambda\!\left[\tfrac12\Delta_\tau^2f(0\mid0)\right]=[\Delta_\tau(P_\lambda f)](0\mid0).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any finite base point and subgradient, the subdifferential of one half of the second-order difference quotient equals the corresponding difference quotient of the subgradient mapping. At a minimizing origin with zero subgradient, formation of the Moreau envelope and proximal mapping also commutes with these difference quotients for every positive quotient and envelope parameter.
assumptions_latex: \text{For the envelope and proximal identities: }\bar x=\bar v=0,\ f(0)=0=\min f,\ \lambda>0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial[\tfrac12\Delta_\tau^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)]=[\Delta_\tau\partial f](\bar x\mid\bar v),\quad e_\lambda[\tfrac12\Delta_\tau^2f(0\mid0)]=[\tfrac12\Delta_\tau^2(e_\lambda f)](0\mid0),\quad P_\lambda[\tfrac12\Delta_\tau^2f(0\mid0)]=[\Delta_\tau(P_\lambda f)](0\mid0).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: indicator specialization of the prox-regular epi-to-proto theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-indicator specialization of subgradient proto-differentiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the stated assumptions, the normal-cone difference quotients
\[
w\mapsto\frac{N_C(\bar x+tw)-\bar v}{t}
\]
graphically converge as \(t\downarrow0\). Therefore \(N_C\) is proto-differentiable at \((\bar x,\bar v)\), and for every \(w\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[
DN_C(\bar x,\bar v)(w)=\partial\!\left(\frac12d_e^2\delta_C(\bar x\mid\bar v)\right)(w).
\]
This identity transfers the second-order feasible geometry encoded by the indicator into the graphical derivative of the normal mapping.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normal-Cone, Projection, and Indicator Proto-Differentiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes projection semidifferentiability through normal-cone proto-differentiability and second epi-differentiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let C\subset\mathbb{R}^n be prox-regular at \bar x for \bar v, and set \bar u=\bar x+\bar v. Then the following are equivalent: (a) N_C is proto-differentiable at \bar x for \bar v; (b) P_C is proto-differentiable at \bar u for \bar x; (c) P_C is single-valued and semidifferentiable at \bar u; (d) \delta_C is twice epi-differentiable at \bar x for \bar v. These properties hold in particular if C is fully amenable at \bar x. When they hold, \[DN_C(\bar x\mid\bar v)=\partial\!\left[\tfrac12d^2\delta_C(\bar x\mid\bar v)\right],\qquad DP_C(\bar u)=[I+DN_C(\bar x\mid\bar v)]^{-1}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a prox-regular set, proto-differentiability of its normal-cone mapping, proto-differentiability of its projection, single-valued semidifferentiability of that projection, and twice epi-differentiability of its indicator are equivalent. They hold for fully amenable sets, and the normal and projection derivatives satisfy the stated subdifferential and resolvent formulas.
assumptions_latex: C\text{ is prox-regular at }\bar x\text{ for }\bar v
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_C\text{ proto-differentiable at }(\bar x,\bar v)\iff P_C\text{ proto-differentiable at }(\bar u,\bar x)\iff P_C\text{ is single-valued and semidifferentiable at }\bar u\iff\delta_C\text{ is twice epi-differentiable at }(\bar x,\bar v),\quad DN_C=\partial[\tfrac12d^2\delta_C],\quad DP_C=(I+DN_C)^{-1}.

children.title: Proximity-Mapping Differentiability
children.top_down_role: Proximity and resolvent consequences of epi-proto correspondence.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) satisfies the hypotheses ensuring the proto-derivative \(D(\partial f)(\bar x,\bar v)\).
\(\lambda>0\), \(\bar y=\bar x+\lambda\bar v\), and the resolvent \((I+\lambda\partial f)^{-1}\) is locally single-valued at \(\bar y\).
For each \(h\), the linearized inclusion has a unique solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_\lambda=(I+\lambda\partial f)^{-1}\) is directionally differentiable at \(\bar y\), with derivative determined by \(h\in w+\lambda D(\partial f)(\bar x,\bar v)(w)\).

notation.meaning: Directional derivative of the proximity mapping.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: directional differentiation of a locally single-valued resolvent of a proto-differentiable mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional derivative of a locally single-valued proximal resolvent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The proximity mapping satisfies
\[
P_\lambda=(I+\lambda\partial f)^{-1},\qquad P_\lambda(\bar y)=\bar x.
\]
Under the stated assumptions, \(P_\lambda\) is directionally differentiable at \(\bar y\). For every input direction \(h\in\mathbb R^n\), its derivative \(w=P_\lambda'(\bar y;h)\) is the unique vector satisfying
\[
h\in w+\lambda D(\partial f)(\bar x,\bar v)(w).
\]
If the epi-to-proto representation applies, the last term may equivalently be replaced by \(\lambda\partial(\tfrac12d_e^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v))(w)\).

children.title: Second Epi-Differentiability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Epigraphical regimes supporting correspondence with mapping-level proto-differentiability.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Twice epi-differentiability means that the second difference quotients epi-converge to the proper function \(d_e^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite-dimensional definition of twice epi-differentiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional definition with denominator \(t^2/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(t>0\), define
\[
\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w):=\frac{f(\bar x+tw)-f(\bar x)-t\langle\bar v,w\rangle}{\tfrac12t^2}.
\]
The function \(f\) is twice epi-differentiable at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\) when there exists a proper lower-semicontinuous function \(q:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) such that
\[
\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)\xrightarrow{e}q\quad\text{as }\(t\downarrow0\).
\]
The limit is denoted by \(q=d_e^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Twice epi-differentiability is epigraphical convergence of normalized second-order difference quotients to a proper lower-semicontinuous model.
knowledge_statements.title: Second Epi-Differentiability Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind are plausible, but no citation supports the selected normalization and proper-limit convention. The second display also nests inline math delimiters inside display math.

children.title: Epi-to-Proto Transfer Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on transferring second epigraphical information to proto-derivative representations.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is defined by \(f(0)=0\) and \(f(x)=x^2\sin(1/x)\) for \(x\neq0\).
The reference pair is \((\bar x,\bar v)=(0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without prox-regularity, a second epi-derivative does not guarantee the proto-derivative identity for \(\partial f\).

notation.meaning: Second-order difference quotient at the reference pair.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oscillatory one-dimensional boundary example illustrating the role of prox-regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(w\neq0\),
\[
\Delta_t^2f(0\mid0)(w)=2w^2\sin\!\left(\frac1{tw}\right),
\]
whose oscillations permit an epigraphical lower model while the nearby derivatives
\[
f'(x)=2x\sin(1/x)-\cos(1/x)
\]
have order-one oscillations as \(x\to0\). Consequently the scaled subgradient graphs need not converge to the subgradient graph of half the second epi-model. Thus twice epi-differentiability alone, after prox-regularity is removed, does not imply the epi-to-proto identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An oscillatory quadratic can possess a second epi-model while its scaled subgradient graphs fail to obey the expected proto-derivative formula.
knowledge_statements.title: Epi-to-Proto Transfer Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The oscillatory calculations alone do not specify the epi-limit or an explicit graphical sequence proving failure of proto-differentiability or of the asserted identity. Because the validity of this particular counterexample is source-sensitive, an exact source or direct verified formulation is required.

children.title: Convex Second-Order Conjugacy
children.top_down_role: Duality between primal and conjugate second-order models.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
Both paired second epi-derivatives exist as proper closed convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\tfrac12d_e^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v))^*=\tfrac12d_e^2f^*(\bar v\mid\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate of a directional model q.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex second-order Fenchel conjugacy under the \(t^2/2\) convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
q(w)=\frac12d_e^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w),
\qquad
q^*(z)=\sup_w\{\langle z,w\rangle-q(w)\}.
\]
Under the stated paired twice epi-differentiability assumptions, the conjugate second-order model is
\[
q^*(z)=\frac12d_e^2f^*(\bar v\mid\bar x)(z)
\quad\text{for every }\(z\in\mathbb R^n\).
\]
Thus primal and conjugate curvature models are Fenchel conjugates after the common factor \(1/2\) dictated by the selected second-difference normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex function and its conjugate, the paired half-scaled second epi-derivatives are Fenchel conjugates.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Second-Order Conjugacy

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second epi-derivative of a conjugate of a fully amenable function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fully amenable primal function yields twice epi-differentiability and an explicit dual supremum representation for the conjugate's second epi-derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose f(x)=\sup_{v}\{\langle v,x\rangle-\varphi(v)\}, where \varphi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}} is lower semicontinuous, proper, and convex, so that \partial f(x)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{v}\{\langle v,x\rangle-\varphi(v)\}. If \bar{v}\in\partial f(\bar{x}) and \varphi is fully amenable at \bar{v}, then f is twice epi-differentiable at \bar{x} for \bar{v}, and for every w, d^2f(\bar{x}\mid\bar{v})(w)=\sup_z\{2\langle w,z\rangle-d^2\varphi(\bar{v}\mid\bar{x})(z)\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a function is represented as the conjugate of a lower-semicontinuous proper convex function that is fully amenable at an active maximizer, then the conjugate is twice epi-differentiable at the associated primal-dual pair. Its second epi-derivative is given by the stated supremum involving the second epi-derivative of the original function.
assumptions_latex: \varphi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\text{ is lower semicontinuous, proper, and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is twice epi-differentiable at }\bar{x}\text{ for }\bar{v},\qquad d^2f(\bar{x}\mid\bar{v})(w)=\sup_z\left\{2\langle w,z\rangle-d^2\varphi(\bar{v}\mid\bar{x})(z)\right\}\quad\forall w.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order epi-differentiability under convex conjugacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of proper twice epi-differentiability for a closed proper convex function and its conjugate, together with conjugacy of their second epi-derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}} be lower semicontinuous, proper, and convex. If \bar{x}\in\operatorname{dom}f and \bar{v}\in\partial f(\bar{x}), then \bar{v}\in\operatorname{dom}f^* and \bar{x}\in\partial f^*(\bar{v}). Moreover, f is properly twice epi-differentiable at \bar{x} for \bar{v} if and only if f^* is properly twice epi-differentiable at \bar{v} for \bar{x}. In that case, \tfrac12 d^2f(\bar{x}\mid\bar{v}) and \tfrac12 d^2f^*(\bar{v}\mid\bar{x}) are convex conjugates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a lower-semicontinuous proper convex function and a primal-dual subgradient pair, proper twice epi-differentiability holds for the function exactly when it holds for its conjugate at the reversed pair. When it holds, one half of their second epi-derivatives are convex conjugates.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\text{ is lower semicontinuous, proper, and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is properly twice epi-differentiable at }\bar{x}\text{ for }\bar{v}\iff f^*\text{ is properly twice epi-differentiable at }\bar{v}\text{ for }\bar{x},\qquad \frac12d^2f(\bar{x}\mid\bar{v})=\left(\frac12d^2f^*(\bar{v}\mid\bar{x})\right)^*.

children.title: Subgradient-Graph Duality
children.top_down_role: Dual interpretation of subgradient proto-derivatives and second epi-derivatives.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(\partial f^*)(\bar v,\bar x)=[D(\partial f)(\bar x,\bar v)]^{-1}\).

notation.meaning: Graphical derivative of the subgradient mapping.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: graphical differentiation of the Fenchel subgradient inverse identity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph-swapping duality for convex subgradient proto-derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fenchel subgradient duality gives
\[
\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\bar x\in\partial f^*(\bar v),
\qquad
(\partial f)^{-1}=\partial f^*.
\]
Swapping the coordinates of the two identical graphs also swaps their tangent directions. Hence
\[
z\in D(\partial f)(\bar x,\bar v)(w)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
w\in D(\partial f^*)(\bar v,\bar x)(z),
\]
or equivalently
\[
D(\partial f^*)(\bar v,\bar x)=[D(\partial f)(\bar x,\bar v)]^{-1}.
\]
When the epi-to-proto theorem applies, these inverse mappings are generated by the paired second epi-models.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex conjugacy swaps subgradient graph coordinates, so the graphical derivatives of the primal and conjugate subgradients are inverse mappings.
knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient-Graph Duality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The graph-inversion identity is standard and the duality content kind fits, but the record supplies no citation and includes a derivational argument rather than only a knowledge statement. An exact source should support the graphical-derivative inverse identity and its scope.

children.title: Primal–Dual Curvature Transfer
children.top_down_role: Transfer of curvature and growth information between conjugate representations.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite-dimensional, and \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(\bar v\in\partial f(\bar x)\), and \(f\) is twice epi-differentiable at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d_e^2 f^*(\bar v\mid\bar x)(z)=2\left(\tfrac12 d_e^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)\right)^*(z).\]

notation.meaning: second epi-derivative with denominator one-half times the squared step

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex conjugacy under the half-square normalization of second difference quotients.

source_refs.locator: 1.3.5 Second-Order Subdifferentials p. 121
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(z\in X\), the second epi-derivative of the conjugate transfers the primal curvature by scaled Fenchel conjugacy:
\[d_e^2 f^*(\bar v\mid\bar x)(z)=2\sup_{w\in X}\left\{\langle z,w\rangle-\tfrac12 d_e^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)\right\}.\]
Thus finiteness, coercivity, and positive quadratic growth of the primal second-order model correspond respectively to domain, smoothness, and reciprocal curvature properties of the dual model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual second-order model is the appropriately scaled Fenchel conjugate of the primal model, transferring growth and curvature information between them.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Curvature Transfer

children.title: Additive Second-Order Calculus
children.top_down_role: Second-order calculus for finite sums of variational functions.

assumptions_latex: \(f_i:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper closed convex functions, and one is continuous at a common domain point.
\(\bar v\in\partial(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i)(\bar x)\), and the functions are twice epi-differentiable for every relevant subgradient decomposition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d_e^2\!\left(\sum_i f_i\right)(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)=\inf_{\substack{v_i\in\partial f_i(\bar x)\\\sum_i v_i=\bar v}}\sum_i d_e^2f_i(\bar x\mid v_i)(w).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex finite-sum rule with minimization over compatible subgradient decompositions.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.5 Second-Order Subdifferential Calculus p. 335
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\) and
\[\mathcal V(\bar x,\bar v)=\{(v_1,\ldots,v_m):v_i\in\partial f_i(\bar x),\ \sum_i v_i=\bar v\}.\]
Then, for every \(w\in X\),
\[d_e^2F(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)=\inf_{(v_i)\in\mathcal V(\bar x,\bar v)}\sum_{i=1}^m d_e^2f_i(\bar x\mid v_i)(w),\]
with the infimum equal to \(+\infty\) when \(\mathcal V(\bar x,\bar v)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The second-order model of a qualified convex sum is the infimum of component models over all subgradients summing to the reference subgradient.
knowledge_statements.title: Additive Second-Order Calculus

children.title: Block-Separable Second-Order Calculus
children.top_down_role: Second-order calculus organized by independent variable blocks or components.

assumptions_latex: \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) and \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\), with each \(f_i\) proper and lower semicontinuous.
Each \(f_i\) is twice epi-differentiable at \(\bar x_i\) for \(\bar v_i\in\partial f_i(\bar x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d_e^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)=\sum_{i=1}^m d_e^2f_i(\bar x_i\mid\bar v_i)(w_i).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact product-space rule for an uncoupled separable extended-real-valued function.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.5 Second-Order Subdifferential Calculus p. 335
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\bar x=(\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_m)\), \(\bar v=(\bar v_1,\ldots,\bar v_m)\), and every \(w=(w_1,\ldots,w_m)\in X\), separability gives
\[d_e^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)=\sum_{i=1}^m d_e^2f_i(\bar x_i\mid\bar v_i)(w_i).\]
Consequently, the effective domain of the product model is the Cartesian product of the component effective domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an uncoupled block-separable function, the second epi-derivative is exactly the sum of the blockwise second epi-derivatives.
knowledge_statements.title: Block-Separable Second-Order Calculus

children.title: Coupled-Sum Qualification Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regularity regimes governing exact additive calculus when components interact.

assumptions_latex: \(f_i:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper lower-semicontinuous functions finite at \(\bar x\).
The limiting-subdifferential qualification \(\{(v_i):v_i\in\partial^\infty f_i(\bar x),\ \sum_i v_i=0\}\subseteq\{(0,\ldots,0)\}\) holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[\partial\!\left(\sum_i f_i\right)(\bar x)\subseteq\sum_i\partial f_i(\bar x),\]
with exact second-order sum rules requiring compatible twice epi-differentiability or second-order regularity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A standard finite-dimensional horizon qualification separating admissible coupled sums from abnormal cancellation.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.5 Second-Order Subdifferential Calculus p. 335
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A coupled finite sum satisfies the basic qualification at \(\bar x\) when
\[v_i\in\partial^\infty f_i(\bar x)\ \text{for all }i,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^m v_i=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad v_i=0\ \text{for all }i.\]
This excludes cancellation of abnormal horizon subgradients. Together with twice epi-differentiability and attainment of a compatible decomposition \(\bar v=\sum_i v_i\), it is a standard regime for exact or inclusion-form second-order sum calculus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sum qualification excludes cancellation among nonzero horizon subgradients; second-order regularity is additionally needed for exact curvature formulas.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled-Sum Qualification Regimes

assumptions_latex: \(F:X\to Y\) is twice continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\), and \(g:Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper closed convex.
\(\bar v\in\partial(g\circ F)(\bar x)\), the multiplier set is nonempty, and the stated composite is twice epi-differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d_e^2(g\circ F)(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)=\inf_{y\in\Lambda(\bar x,\bar v)}\left[d_e^2g(F(\bar x)\mid y)(F'(\bar x)w)+\langle y,F''(\bar x)[w,w]\rangle\right].\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[\Lambda(\bar x,\bar v)=\{y\in\partial g(F(\bar x)):F'(\bar x)^*y=\bar v\}.\]
Under a composite qualification ensuring exactness, every \(w\in X\) satisfies
\[d_e^2(g\circ F)(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)=\inf_{y\in\Lambda(\bar x,\bar v)}\left\{d_e^2g(F(\bar x)\mid y)(F'(\bar x)w)+\langle y,F''(\bar x)[w,w]\rangle\right\}.\]
The two terms represent transported outer curvature and curvature of the inner mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite curvature is outer curvature along the linearized image plus the multiplier-weighted second derivative of the smooth inner mapping.

assumptions_latex: \(F:X\times Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper lower semicontinuous, and \(\varphi(x)=\inf_y F(x,y)\).
\(\bar y\in\operatorname{argmin}_yF(\bar x,y)\), \((\bar v,0)\in\partial F(\bar x,\bar y)\), and localized minimizers are inner-semicompact.
The required twice epi-differentiability and infimum-attainment conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d_e^2\varphi(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)=\inf_{z\in Y}d_e^2F((\bar x,\bar y)\mid(\bar v,0))(w,z).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact second-order marginalization through minimization over eliminated-variable directions.

source_refs.locator: 4.4 Sensitivity Analysis for Variational Systems p. 421
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an active minimizer \(\bar y\) satisfying \((\bar v,0)\in\partial F(\bar x,\bar y)\). Under stability and exactness assumptions preventing loss of minimizing sequences, every \(w\in X\) satisfies
\[d_e^2\varphi(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)=\inf_{z\in Y}d_e^2F((\bar x,\bar y)\mid(\bar v,0))(w,z).\]
If several active minimizers or compatible subgradients occur, the right-hand side is further minimized over those admissible pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The marginal function's second-order model is obtained by minimizing the joint second-order model over directions of the eliminated variable.
knowledge_statements.title: Marginal-Function Second-Order Calculus

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4 Sensitivity Analysis for Variational Systems p. 421
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

The later prose acknowledges an additional minimization that is absent from the displayed conclusion, and the exact stability and attainment assumptions are not stated.

children.title: Value-Function Second-Order Calculus
children.top_down_role: Second-order variational structure of parameterized optimal-value mappings.

assumptions_latex: \(X=\mathbb R^n\), \(Y=\mathbb R^p\), and \(F:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\) is twice continuously differentiable near \((\bar x,\bar y)\).
\(\nabla_yF(\bar x,\bar y)=0\), and \(\nabla_{yy}^2F(\bar x,\bar y)\) is positive definite.
For all \(x\) near \(\bar x\), the local minimization problem near \(\bar y\) has the unique minimizer \(y(x)\), with \(y(\bar x)=\bar y\), and \(V(x)=F(x,y(x))\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[
abla^2V( ar x)=
abla_{xx}^2F( ar x, ar y)-
abla_{xy}^2F( ar x, ar y) igl(
abla_{yy}^2F( ar x, ar y) igr)^{-1}
abla_{yx}^2F( ar x, ar y).\]

notation.meaning: local value function obtained by eliminating the unique local minimizer
Hessian blocks of the joint objective with respect to variables a and b

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional local value-function Hessian under positive-definite curvature in the eliminated variable.

source_refs.locator: 4.2 Second-Order Directional Derivatives p. 162

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The implicit function theorem gives a continuously differentiable local minimizer mapping \(y(\cdot)\), and the local value function \(V(x)=F(x,y(x))\) is twice differentiable at \( ar x\). Its gradient and Hessian satisfy \(
abla V( ar x)=
abla_xF( ar x, ar y)\) and
\[
abla^2V( ar x)=
abla_{xx}^2F( ar x, ar y)-
abla_{xy}^2F( ar x, ar y) igl(
abla_{yy}^2F( ar x, ar y) igr)^{-1}
abla_{yx}^2F( ar x, ar y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth finite-dimensional problem with a locally unique strongly stable inner minimizer, the local value-function Hessian is the Schur complement of the eliminated-variable Hessian block.
knowledge_statements.title: Value-Function Second-Order Calculus

children.title: Parameter-Elimination Stability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes preserving second-order information under elimination of decision variables.

assumptions_latex: The stationarity mapping \(y\mapsto\partial_yF(\bar x,y)\) is strongly metrically regular at \((\bar y,0)\), uniformly under nearby parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[S(x)\cap U=\{y(x)\},\qquad \|y(x)-\bar y\|\le L\|x-\bar x\|\] for nearby \(x\), enabling stable second-order parameter elimination.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong metric regularity regime ensuring single-valued Lipschitz elimination of a minimizing parameter.

source_refs.locator: 4.4 Sensitivity Analysis for Variational Systems p. 421
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A stable parameter-elimination regime holds when the generalized stationarity equation
\[0\in\partial_yF(x,y)\]
is strongly metrically regular at \((\bar x,\bar y,0)\), with localization uniform in \(x\). Then neighborhoods and \(L>0\) exist such that
\[S(x)\cap U=\{y(x)\},\qquad \|y(x)-\bar y\|\le L\|x-\bar x\|\]
for nearby \(x\). This stability controls minimizing sequences used in marginal second-order limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong metric regularity makes the local minimizing parameter unique and Lipschitz, preventing unstable minimizer switching during second-order elimination.
knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Elimination Stability Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4 Sensitivity Analysis for Variational Systems p. 421
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the stability-regime leaf, but strong metric regularity of a stationarity mapping yields a localized stationary solution, not automatically a unique localized argmin. Prox-regularity, tilt stability, second-order sufficiency, or equivalent assumptions are needed to connect the stationarity selection to the minimizer mapping used in the conclusion.

children.title: Indicator-Function Second-Order Calculus
children.top_down_role: Second-order calculus for indicator representations of feasible sets.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset X\) is closed, \(\bar x\in C\), and \(\bar v\in N_C(\bar x)\).
\(C\) is parabolically derivable and parabolically regular at \((\bar x,\bar v)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d_e^2\delta_C(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)=\begin{cases}-\sigma_{T_C^2(\bar x,w)}(\bar v),&w\in T_C(\bar x)\cap\bar v^\perp,\\+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]

notation.meaning: second-order tangent set in direction w

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parabolically regular set formula under the half-square second-difference normalization.

source_refs.locator: 1.3.5 Second-Order Subdifferentials p. 121
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K_C(\bar x,\bar v)=T_C(\bar x)\cap\bar v^\perp\). Under parabolic regularity, the indicator's second epi-derivative is
\[d_e^2\delta_C(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)=
\begin{cases}
-\sigma_{T_C^2(\bar x,w)}(\bar v),&w\in K_C(\bar x,\bar v),\\
+\infty,&w\notin K_C(\bar x,\bar v).
\end{cases}\]
Thus indicator curvature is the negative support of feasible second-order corrections, restricted to critical first-order directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Indicator curvature is finite only on the critical cone and there equals the negative support of feasible second-order tangent corrections.
knowledge_statements.title: Indicator-Function Second-Order Calculus

children.title: Distance-Function Second-Order Calculus
children.top_down_role: Second-order calculus for distance-based representations of set geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(h(x)=\tfrac12 d_C(x)^2\).
The metric projection \(P_C\) is directionally differentiable at \(\bar x\) in direction \(w\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[h''(\bar x;w)=\langle w,w-P_C'(\bar x;w)\rangle.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second directional derivative of the squared distance to a closed convex set.

source_refs.locator: 4.2 Second-Order Directional Derivatives p. 162

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty closed convex set, \(P_C\) is single-valued and
\[\nabla h(x)=x-P_C(x),\qquad h(x)=\tfrac12 d_C(x)^2.\]
If \(P_C'(\bar x;w)\) exists, then the second directional derivative of \(h\) exists and satisfies
\[h''(\bar x;w)=\langle w,w-P_C'(\bar x;w)\rangle.\]
Hence the second-order behavior of squared distance is determined by the directional sensitivity of the metric projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The squared-distance curvature equals the direction paired with its residual after differentiating the metric projection.
knowledge_statements.title: Distance-Function Second-Order Calculus

children.title: Set–Function Geometry Transfer
children.top_down_role: Passage between second-order feasible-set geometry plus function-based representations.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is closed and parabolically derivable at \(\bar x\in C\) in direction \(w\).
\(v\in N_C(\bar x)\), \(\langle v,w\rangle=0\), and the indicator \(\delta_C\) is twice epi-differentiable at \(\bar x\) for \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d^2\delta_C(\bar x\mid v)(w)=-\sigma_{T_C^2(\bar x,w)}(v).\]

notation.meaning: indicator function of the set C
second-order tangent set to C at x-bar in direction w

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional indicator-function transfer under parabolic regularity.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.5 Second-Order Subdifferential Calculus p. 335
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the indicator \(\delta_C\), define the second subderivative by \[d^2\delta_C(\bar x\mid v)(w):=\liminf_{\substack{t\downarrow0\\w'\to w}}\frac{\delta_C(\bar x+tw')-\delta_C(\bar x)-t\langle v,w'\rangle}{\tfrac12t^2}.\] Under the stated regularity, feasible parabolic arcs transfer this functional quantity to set geometry: \[d^2\delta_C(\bar x\mid v)(w)=\inf_{z\in T_C^2(\bar x,w)}-\langle v,z\rangle=-\sigma_{T_C^2(\bar x,w)}(v).\] If the second-order tangent set is empty, the infimum is \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The indicator's second subderivative equals the negative support of the second-order tangent set, transferring second-order set geometry into function geometry.
knowledge_statements.title: Set–Function Geometry Transfer

children.title: Second-Subderivative Calculus Architecture
children.top_down_role: Organization of primal second-subderivative calculus across standard function operations.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous, \(f(\bar x)<+\infty\), and \(v\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d^2f(\bar x\mid v)=\operatorname*{e\!\!-\!liminf}_{t\downarrow0}\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid v),\] with exact calculus requiring equality of the corresponding epigraphical limits.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Difference-quotient architecture for primal second-order rules.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.5 Second-Order Subdifferential Calculus p. 335
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(t>0\), set \[\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w):=\frac{f(\bar x+tw)-f(\bar x)-t\langle v,w\rangle}{\tfrac12t^2}.\] The second subderivative is the lower epigraphical limit \[d^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w)=\liminf_{\substack{t\downarrow0\\w'\to w}}\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w').\] Consequently, a second-subderivative calculus rule is obtained by transforming these quotients and passing to an epigraphical lower limit; an exact rule additionally requires matching recovery sequences, equivalently the corresponding epigraphical upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Second-subderivative calculus transforms second-order difference quotients and passes to epigraphical limits; exactness additionally requires recovery sequences.
knowledge_statements.title: Second-Subderivative Calculus Architecture

children.title: Epi-Derivative Calculus Architecture
children.top_down_role: Organization of epigraphical second-order calculus across standard function operations.

knowledge_statements.title: Epi-Derivative Calculus Architecture
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential finite-dimensional definition of proper twice epi-differentiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(t>0\), define \[\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w):=\frac{f(\bar x+tw)-f(\bar x)-t\langle v,w\rangle}{\tfrac12t^2}.\] The function \(f\) is properly twice epi-differentiable at \(\bar x\) for \(v\) when these quotients epigraphically converge as \(t\downarrow0\) to a proper extended-real function \(d_e^2f(\bar x\mid v)\). Equivalently, the epigraphical lower bound holds along every convergent sequence, and each \(w\in\mathbb{R}^n\) admits a recovery sequence attaining the matching upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proper twice epi-differentiability means that the second-order difference quotients epi-converge to a proper second epi-derivative.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous, \(f(\bar x)<+\infty\), and \(v\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\Delta_t^2f(\bar x\mid v)\xrightarrow{e}d_e^2f(\bar x\mid v)\quad\text{as }t\downarrow0,\] where \(d_e^2f(\bar x\mid v)\) is proper.

children.title: Finite-Sum Calculus
children.top_down_role: Finite additive structures and qualification-sensitive exactness.

assumptions_latex: \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) are proper lower semicontinuous functions, and \(\bar v\in\partial(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i)(\bar x)\).
The limiting-subdifferential sum rule and its coderivative qualification hold at every decomposition \((v_1,\ldots,v_m)\) with \(v_i\in\partial f_i(\bar x)\) and \(\sum_i v_i=\bar v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial^2\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\right)(\bar x,\bar v)(u)\subseteq\bigcup_{(v_i)\in\Lambda(\bar x,\bar v)}\sum_{i=1}^m\partial^2f_i(\bar x,v_i)(u).\]

notation.meaning: limiting second-order subdifferential, defined as the coderivative of the limiting subgradient mapping

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limiting second-order subdifferential inclusion for finite sums.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.5 Second-Order Subdifferential Calculus p. 335
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\) and define \[\Lambda(\bar x,\bar v):=\left\{(v_1,\ldots,v_m):v_i\in\partial f_i(\bar x),\ \sum_{i=1}^m v_i=\bar v\right\}.\] Under the stated first- and second-order qualifications, for every \(u\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[\partial^2F(\bar x,\bar v)(u)\subseteq\bigcup_{(v_i)\in\Lambda(\bar x,\bar v)}\left(\partial^2f_1(\bar x,v_1)(u)+\cdots+\partial^2f_m(\bar x,v_m)(u)\right).\] Equality requires additional regularity and is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under compatible first- and second-order qualifications, the second-order subdifferential of a finite sum is contained in sums over all subgradient decompositions.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Sum Calculus

children.title: Smooth-Perturbation Calculus
children.top_down_role: Generalized Hessian behavior under smooth perturbations.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous, \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is \(C^2\) near \(\bar x\), and \(v\in\partial(f+g)(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\partial^2(f+g)(\bar x,v)(u)=\nabla^2g(\bar x)u+\partial^2f\bigl(\bar x,v-\nabla g(\bar x)\bigr)(u).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact limiting generalized-Hessian rule for a smooth additive perturbation.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.5 Second-Order Subdifferential Calculus p. 335
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Put \(v_f:=v-\nabla g(\bar x)\). Then \(v_f\in\partial f(\bar x)\), and the smooth translation of the subgradient graph yields, for every \(u\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[\partial^2(f+g)(\bar x,v)(u)=\nabla^2g(\bar x)u+\partial^2f(\bar x,v_f)(u).\] Thus the classical Hessian of the perturbation enters additively, while all nonsmooth second-order behavior remains in the second-order subdifferential of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a twice continuously differentiable function translates the second-order subdifferential exactly by its Hessian applied to the direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Smooth-Perturbation Calculus

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-Order Chain Rule with a Lipschitz Inner Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A second-order subdifferential inclusion for a Lipschitz inner mapping and a \(C^{1,1}\) outer function on Asplund spaces, including the strict-differentiability exception for the outer space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar y\in\partial(\varphi\circ g)(\bar x)\), where \(g:X\to Z\) is Lipschitz continuous around \(\bar x\), \(\varphi:Z\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is \(C^{1,1}\) around \(\bar z:=g(\bar x)\), and \(\bar v:=\nabla\varphi(\bar z)\). Suppose \(X,X^*,Z,Z^*\) are Asplund and the graph of \((x,v)\mapsto\partial\langle v,h\rangle(x)\) is norm-closed in \(X\times Z^*\times X^*\) near \((\bar x,\bar v)\). Then, for every \(u\in X^{**}\), \[\partial^2(\varphi\circ g)(\bar x,\bar y)(u)\subset\bigcup_{(x^*,v^*)\in D^2g(\bar x,\bar v,\bar y)(u)}\left[x^*+D_N^*g(\bar x)\circ\partial_N^2\varphi(\bar z)(v^*)\right],\] with corresponding normal or mixed second-order constructions. The inclusion remains valid for an arbitrary Banach space \(Z\) if \(\nabla\varphi\) is strictly differentiable at \(\bar z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the inner mapping is locally Lipschitz, the outer function is continuously differentiable with locally Lipschitz derivative, the stated Asplund and graph-closedness assumptions hold, then the normal or mixed second-order subdifferential of the composition is bounded above by a union combining the inner mapping's second-order derivative and coderivative with the outer function's normal second-order subdifferential. The requirement that the outer space be Asplund can be dropped when the outer gradient is strictly differentiable at the reference point.
assumptions_latex: \(g:X\to Z\) is Lipschitz continuous around \(\bar x\).
\(\varphi:Z\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is \(C^{1,1}\) around \(\bar z=g(\bar x)\), with \(\bar v=\nabla\varphi(\bar z)\).
\(X,X^*,Z,Z^*\) are Asplund spaces, except that \(Z\) may be an arbitrary Banach space when \(\nabla\varphi\) is strictly differentiable at \(\bar z\).
The graph of \((x,v)\mapsto\partial\langle v,h\rangle(x)\) is norm-closed in \(X\times Z^*\times X^*\) for \((x,v)\) near \((\bar x,\bar v)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial^2(\varphi\circ g)(\bar x,\bar y)(u)\subset\displaystyle\bigcup_{(x^*,v^*)\in D^2g(\bar x,\bar v,\bar y)(u)}[x^*+D_N^*g(\bar x)\circ\partial_N^2\varphi(\bar z)(v^*)]\) for the corresponding normal or mixed second-order constructions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Chain Rule for Second Subderivatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite second-subderivative lower bound, exactness under full amenability, and the piecewise linear-quadratic specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f=g\circ F\), where \(F:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R^m\) is \(C^2\), \(g:\mathbb R^m	o\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper and lsc, and \(g\) is finite and regular at \(F( ar x)\). Assume \[y\in\partial^\infty g(F( ar x)),\quad 
abla(yF)( ar x)=0\Longrightarrow y=0.\] For \(v\in\partial f( ar x)\), define \[Y( ar x,v)=\{y\in\partial g(F( ar x)):
abla(yF)( ar x)=v\}.\] This set is nonempty, compact, and convex, and for every \(w\in\mathbb R^n\), \[d^2f( ar x\mid v)(w)\ge \sup_{y\in Y( ar x,v)}\left[d^2g(F( ar x)\mid y)(
abla F( ar x)w)+\langle w,
abla^2(yF)( ar x)wangleight].\] Equality holds when \(g\) is fully amenable at \(F( ar x)\); then \(f\) is properly twice epi-differentiable and \[\operatorname{dom}d^2f( ar x\mid v)=\{w:df( ar x)(w)=\langle v,wangle\}=N_{\partial f( ar x)}(v).\] If \(g\) is convex piecewise linear-quadratic, then with \( ar f(x)=g(F( ar x)+
abla F( ar x)(x- ar x))\), \[d^2f( ar x\mid v)(w)=d^2 ar f( ar x\mid v)(w)+\max_{y\in Y( ar x,v)}\langle w,
abla^2(yF)( ar x)wangle,\] where \( ar f\) is convex piecewise linear-quadratic and has the same value, first subderivative, and subdifferential as \(f\) at \( ar x\); moreover \(d^2 ar f( ar x\mid v)(w)=d^2g(F( ar x)\mid y)(
abla F( ar x)w)\) for every \(y\in Y( ar x,v)\), equivalently it equals \(d^2g(F( ar x))(
abla F( ar x)w)\) when \(dg(F( ar x))(
abla F( ar x)w)=\langle v,wangle\), and \(+\infty\) otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a qualified smooth composite, the multiplier set representing a chosen subgradient is nonempty, compact, and convex. The second subderivative is bounded below by the supremum of the outer second subderivative plus the curvature term. Full amenability makes the rule exact and yields proper twice epi-differentiability and the stated domain formula. A convex piecewise linear-quadratic outer function gives the more explicit linearized-composite representation.

For a single-valued \(C^1\) mapping, the tangent cone to its graph is the graph of its Jacobian. Consequently, for every \(h\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[
D(F+G)(\bar x)(h)=\{(\nabla F(\bar x)+\nabla G(\bar x))h\},
\]
and
\[
D(Q\circ F)(\bar x)(h)=\{\nabla Q(F(\bar x))\nabla F(\bar x)h\}.
\]
Thus the graphical-derivative sum and composition rules are exact in this smooth single-valued regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For continuously differentiable single-valued mappings, graphical derivatives are ordinary Jacobian actions, so both the sum rule and chain rule hold with equality.

knowledge_statements.title: Coderivative Sum Calculus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional limiting-coderivative sum rule with decomposition compactness and normal qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H(x):=F(x)+G(x)\), let \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}H\), and define
\[
S(x,y):=\{(y_1,y_2)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^m\mid y_1\in F(x),\ y_2\in G(x),\ y_1+y_2=y\}.
\]
If the stated assumptions hold, then for every \(y^*\in\mathbb R^m\),
\[
D^*H(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)\subseteq
\bigcup_{(y_1,y_2)\in S(\bar x,\bar y)}
\left[D^*F(\bar x,y_1)(y^*)+D^*G(\bar x,y_2)(y^*)\right].
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the decomposition mapping is inner semicompact and the normal qualification holds at every decomposition of the reference sum value, the coderivative of the sum is contained in the union of the corresponding sums of component coderivatives.
assumptions_latex: The decomposition mapping \(S(x,y):=\{(y_1,y_2)\mid y_1\in F(x),\ y_2\in G(x),\ y_1+y_2=y\}\) is inner semicompact at \((\bar x,\bar y)\).
For every \((y_1,y_2)\in S(\bar x,\bar y)\), the graphs of \(F\) and \(G\) are locally closed near \((\bar x,y_1)\) and \((\bar x,y_2)\), respectively.
For every \((y_1,y_2)\in S(\bar x,\bar y)\), \(D^*F(\bar x,y_1)(0)\cap[-D^*G(\bar x,y_2)(0)]=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D^*(F+G)(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)\subseteq\bigcup_{(y_1,y_2)\in S(\bar x,\bar y)}[D^*F(\bar x,y_1)(y^*)+D^*G(\bar x,y_2)(y^*)]\) for every \(y^*\in\mathbb R^m\).

notation.meaning: Limiting coderivative at the indicated graph point.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\) and \(G:\mathbb R^m\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^p\) have locally closed graphs.
The intermediate-point mapping \(M(x,z):=F(x)\cap G^{-1}(z)\) is inner semicompact at \((\bar x,\bar z)\).
For every \(\bar y\in M(\bar x,\bar z)\), \(D^*G(\bar y,\bar z)(0)\cap\ker D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D^*(G\circ F)(\bar x,\bar z)(z^*)\subseteq\bigcup_{\bar y\in M(\bar x,\bar z)}D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(D^*G(\bar y,\bar z)(z^*))\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H:=G\circ F\) and \((\bar x,\bar z)\in\operatorname{gph}H\). Under the stated assumptions, for every \(z^*\in\mathbb R^p\),
\[
D^*H(\bar x,\bar z)(z^*)
\subseteq
\bigcup_{\bar y\in M(\bar x,\bar z)}
\bigcup_{y^*\in D^*G(\bar y,\bar z)(z^*)}
D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*).
\]
Thus each output covector is propagated first through \(G\) and then through \(F\), with a union over admissible intermediate points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A qualified coderivative chain rule propagates covectors backward through the outer and inner multifunctions, accounting for every locally relevant intermediate point.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a single-valued \(C^1\) mapping, its limiting coderivative is exactly the transpose Jacobian. Hence, for every \(y^*\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(z^*\in\mathbb R^p\),
\[
D^*(F+G)(\bar x)(y^*)=\{(\nabla F(\bar x)+\nabla G(\bar x))^\top y^*\},
\]
and
\[
D^*(Q\circ F)(\bar x)(z^*)=\{\nabla F(\bar x)^\top\nabla Q(F(\bar x))^\top z^*\}.
\]
Thus both coderivative calculus inclusions become equalities in the smooth single-valued regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For continuously differentiable single-valued mappings, coderivatives are transpose Jacobians, and the coderivative sum and chain rules are exact.

knowledge_statements.title: Inverse-Mapping Derivative Calculus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact graphical-derivative inversion identity in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\) and \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\). For every \(k\in\mathbb R^m\),
\[
DF^{-1}(\bar y,\bar x)(k)
=
\{h\in\mathbb R^n\mid k\in DF(\bar x,\bar y)(h)\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(h\in DF^{-1}(\bar y,\bar x)(k)\) if and only if \((h,k)\in T_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,\bar y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The graphical derivative of an inverse multifunction is obtained exactly by exchanging the input and output direction coordinates in the original graphical derivative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(DF^{-1}(\bar y,\bar x)(k)=\{h\in\mathbb R^n\mid k\in DF(\bar x,\bar y)(h)\}\) for every \(k\in\mathbb R^m\).

notation.meaning: Graphical derivative at the specified graph point.

assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb R^q\times\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is \(C^1\) near \((\bar p,\bar x)\) and \(g(\bar p,\bar x)=0\).
\(\nabla_x g(\bar p,\bar x):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is surjective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(DS(\bar p,\bar x)(d)=\{u\in\mathbb R^n\mid \nabla_p g(\bar p,\bar x)d+\nabla_x g(\bar p,\bar x)u=0\}\).

notation.meaning: Solution multifunction of the parameterized equation.
Graphical derivative of the solution mapping.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth equation specialization under a surjective state Jacobian.

source_refs.locator: 4.4 Sensitivity Analysis for Variational Systems p. 421
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(S(p):=\{x\in\mathbb R^n\mid g(p,x)=0\}\). The surjectivity assumption makes the local zero set a smooth manifold. For every parameter direction \(d\in\mathbb R^q\), its solution-map graphical derivative is
\[
DS(\bar p,\bar x)(d)
=
\{u\in\mathbb R^n\mid
\nabla_p g(\bar p,\bar x)d+
\nabla_x g(\bar p,\bar x)u=0\}.
\]
Thus admissible solution velocities are precisely the solutions of the linearized implicit equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a surjective state Jacobian, the derivative of an implicit solution mapping consists exactly of velocities satisfying the linearized equation.
knowledge_statements.title: Implicit-Mapping Derivative Calculus

assumptions_latex: \(S:\mathbb R^q\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n\) has locally closed graph near \((\bar p,\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) has the Aubin property around \((\bar p,\bar x)\) if and only if \(D^*S(\bar p,\bar x)(0)=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: Limiting coderivative of the solution mapping.

source_refs.locator: 4.4 Sensitivity Analysis for Variational Systems p. 421

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The mapping \(S\) has the Aubin property around \((\bar p,\bar x)\), meaning that there are neighborhoods \(U,V\) and \(L\geq0\) such that
\[
S(p_1)\cap V\subseteq S(p_2)+L\|p_1-p_2\|\mathbb B
\quad\text{for all }p_1,p_2\in U,
\]
if and only if the coderivative kernel condition
\[
D^*S(\bar p,\bar x)(0)=\{0\}
\]
holds. This characterizes the locally Lipschitz-like solution-mapping regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally closed solution mapping is Lipschitz-like exactly when its limiting coderivative maps the zero covector only to zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every direction \(u\in\mathbb R^n\), the limiting second-order subdifferential of \(f\) at \(\bar x\) is the singleton
\[
\partial^2 f(\bar x)(u)
:=D^*(\nabla f)(\bar x)(u)
=\{\nabla^2 f(\bar x)u\}.
\]
Hence all coderivative-based second-order information reduces to multiplication by the classical symmetric Hessian in the twice continuously differentiable regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a twice continuously differentiable function, the generalized second-order subdifferential is exactly the classical Hessian applied to the direction.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial_C^2 f(\bar x)(u)=\{Au\mid A\in\partial_C(\nabla f)(\bar x)\}\) for every \(u\in\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: Clarke generalized Jacobian of the locally Lipschitz gradient.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clarke generalized-Hessian representation for locally Lipschitz gradients.

source_refs.locator: 7.1 Nonsmooth Analysis I: Clarke's Calculus p. 626
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Since \(\nabla f\) is locally Lipschitz, it is differentiable almost everywhere. Its Clarke generalized Hessian is
\[
\partial_C(\nabla f)(\bar x)
=
\operatorname{co}\left\{\lim_{k\to\infty}\nabla^2f(x_k)
\mid x_k\to\bar x,\ \nabla f\text{ is differentiable at }x_k\right\}.
\]
For every \(u\in\mathbb R^n\), the associated second-order action is
\[
\partial_C^2 f(\bar x)(u)
=
\{Au\mid A\in\partial_C(\nabla f)(\bar x)\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a function with locally Lipschitz gradient, generalized Hessian actions are obtained by applying convexified limiting classical Hessians to the direction.
knowledge_statements.title: C1,1 Functions

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegativity of the second subderivative for proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(w\in\mathbb R^n\), define
\[
d^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)
:=
\liminf_{\substack{t\downarrow0\\w'\to w}}
\frac{f(\bar x+tw')-f(\bar x)-t\langle\bar v,w'\rangle}{\tfrac12t^2}.
\]
Then
\[
d^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)\geq0
\quad\text{for every }w\in\mathbb R^n.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper lower-semicontinuous convex function and any selected convex subgradient, the second subderivative is nonnegative in every direction.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)\geq0\) for every \(w\in\mathbb R^n\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Properties of the gauge of a convex set containing the origin in its interior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sublinearity, local regularity, and level-set representation of the gauge of a convex set containing the origin in its interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a convex subset of a normed space \(X\) with \(0\in\operatorname{int}C\), and let \(g\) be its gauge. Then: (a) \(g:X\to[0,\infty)\); (b) \(g(tx)=t g(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) and \(t\ge0\); (c) \(g(x+y)\le g(x)+g(y)\) for all \(x,y\in X\); (d) \(g\) is locally Lipschitz, hence continuous; and (e) \(\operatorname{int}C=\{x:g(x)<1\}\subseteq C\subseteq\{x:g(x)\le1\}=\operatorname{cl}C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gauge of a convex set containing the origin in its interior is finite and nonnegative, positively homogeneous, subadditive, locally Lipschitz, and continuous. Its strict unit sublevel set is the interior of the set, and its closed unit sublevel set is the closure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g\ge0,\quad g(tx)=tg(x)\ (t\ge0),\quad g(x+y)\le g(x)+g(y),\quad g\text{ is locally Lipschitz},\quad \operatorname{int}C=\{g<1\}\subseteq C\subseteq\{g\le1\}=\operatorname{cl}C

children.title: Convex Piecewise-Linear Functions
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral epigraph and critical-face geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and piecewise linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)=\delta_{K_f(\bar x,\bar v)}\).

notation.meaning: Critical cone determined by the directional derivative and subgradient.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical-cone formula for the second subderivative of a convex piecewise-linear function.

source_refs.locator: I.* Piecewise Linear Functions p. 67

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the critical cone
\[
K_f(\bar x,\bar v)
:=\{w\in\mathbb R^n\mid f'(\bar x;w)=\langle\bar v,w\rangle\}.
\]
Then the second subderivative has the exact polyhedral representation
\[
d^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)
=
\delta_{K_f(\bar x,\bar v)}(w)
=
\begin{cases}
0,&w\in K_f(\bar x,\bar v),\\
+\infty,&w\notin K_f(\bar x,\bar v).
\end{cases}
\]
Thus its finite directions are precisely the critical directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex piecewise-linear function, the second subderivative is zero on the critical cone and infinite outside it.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Piecewise-Linear Functions

source_witnesses.locator: I.* Piecewise Linear Functions p. 67

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(t>0\), set
\[
\Delta_t^2f(w):=
\frac{f(\bar x+tw)-f(\bar x)-t\langle\bar v,w\rangle}{\tfrac12t^2}.
\]
As \(t\downarrow0\), these functions epi-converge to \(d^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)\); hence \(f\) is twice epi-differentiable at \(\bar x\) for \(\bar v\). Moreover, \(d^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)\) is a proper lower-semicontinuous convex piecewise linear-quadratic function, so its finite second-order geometry is described by finitely many polyhedral quadratic pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex piecewise linear-quadratic function is twice epi-differentiable, and its second subderivative remains a proper convex piecewise linear-quadratic function.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order structure of convex piecewise linear-quadratic functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second subderivatives, critical-cone representation, differentiability regimes, and local exact expansions for convex PLQ functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}} is proper, convex, and piecewise linear-quadratic, and let \bar x\in\operatorname{dom}f. Then d^2f(\bar x) is proper and piecewise linear-quadratic, though not necessarily convex, and for every w,
\[
d^2f(\bar x)(w)=\lim_{\tau\searrow0}\Delta_\tau^2f(\bar x)(w)=f''(\bar x;w)\geq0.
\]
For every v\in\partial f(\bar x), define the polyhedral critical cone
\[
K(\bar x,v)=\{w:df(\bar x)(w)=\langle v,w\rangle\}.
\]
Then d^2f(\bar x\mid v) is proper, convex, and piecewise linear-quadratic, and
\[
d^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w)=\lim_{\tau\searrow0}\Delta_\tau^2f(\bar x\mid v)(w)=d^2f(\bar x)(w)+\delta_{K(\bar x,v)}(w).
\]
The function is twice epi-differentiable at \bar x for every v\in\partial f(\bar x). It is twice semidifferentiable when \bar x\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f), but not when \bar x\in\operatorname{bdry}(\operatorname{dom}f). Nevertheless, some neighborhood V of \bar x satisfies
\[
f(x)=f(\bar x)+df(\bar x)(x-\bar x)+\tfrac12d^2f(\bar x)(x-\bar x),\qquad x\in V\cap\operatorname{dom}f.
\]
Furthermore, for some \varepsilon>0, every w\in T_{\operatorname{dom}f}(\bar x)\cap\mathbb B, \tau\in(0,\varepsilon), and z\in\mathbb{R}^n satisfy
\[
df(\bar x+\tau w)(z)=d h_1(w)(z)+\tfrac12\tau\,d h_2(w)(z),\qquad h_1=df(\bar x),\quad h_2=d^2f(\bar x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper convex piecewise linear-quadratic function, the ordinary second subderivative is proper and PLQ, may be nonconvex, is nonnegative, and is obtained by fixed-direction limits. Relative to any subgradient, the second subderivative is proper convex PLQ and equals the ordinary second subderivative plus the indicator of the polyhedral critical cone. Twice epi-differentiability always holds for subgradients; twice semidifferentiability holds at interior domain points and fails at boundary points. Exact local second-order function and directional-derivative expansions still hold on the domain.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second directional derivative of a piecewise-C2 function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-piece evaluation of second directional derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be \(\mathrm{PC}^2\) on an open set \(\mathcal O\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), with finitely many \(C^2\) selections \(f_i\) and corresponding pieces \(\mathcal P^i\). Then \(f\) is twice directionally differentiable throughout \(\mathcal O\). For every \((x,d)\in\mathcal O\times\mathbb R^n\), \[f^{(2)}(x;d)=d^\top\nabla^2 f_i(x)d\qquad\forall i\in\mathcal A'(x;d).\] Equivalently, this formula holds for every piece \(\mathcal P^i\) containing \(x\) such that \(d\in\mathcal R(x;\mathcal P^i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finitely piecewise-C2 function is twice directionally differentiable. Its second directional derivative is the quadratic form of the Hessian of any selection active along the direction, equivalently of any containing piece whose radial cone includes that direction.

children.title: Polyhedral Normal-Cone Mappings
children.top_down_role: Critical-face representations for polyhedral systems.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty convex polyhedral set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(DN_C(\bar x,\bar v)(w)=N_K(w)\) for every \(w\in\mathbb{R}^n\).

notation.meaning: Critical cone at the reference normal pair.
Graphical derivative of the normal-cone mapping.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex-polyhedral graphical-derivative formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, convex, and polyhedral, and let \((\bar x,\bar v)\in\operatorname{gph}N_C\). Define the critical cone by \(K:=T_C(\bar x)\cap\bar v^\perp\). Then the graphical derivative of the convex normal-cone mapping has the exact representation
\[
DN_C(\bar x,\bar v)(w)=N_K(w)\qquad(w\in\mathbb{R}^n),
\]
where \(N_K(w)=\varnothing\) when \(w\notin K\). Thus evaluating the first-order graphical variation of \(N_C\), which supplies a basic second-order object for \(\delta_C\), reduces to evaluating normals to the polyhedral critical cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The graphical derivative of a polyhedral normal-cone mapping is exactly the normal-cone mapping of its critical cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Normal-Cone Mappings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is standard and fits the polyhedral-normal-cone leaf, but no source or inspectable locator is cited.

children.title: Smooth Nonlinear Constraint Systems
children.top_down_role: Multiplier and critical-cone evaluation for smooth constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^q\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^q\) is convex polyhedral.
The constraint system \(G(x)\in D\) is nondegenerate at \(\bar x\), and the multiplier associated with \(\bar v\) is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(DN_\Gamma(\bar x,\bar v)(w)=\nabla^2\langle\bar\lambda,G\rangle(\bar x)w+N_K(w)\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set of the smooth constraint system.
Unique multiplier satisfying the normal representation.
Critical cone of the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nondegenerate smooth constraints with a polyhedral target and unique multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Gamma:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:G(x)\in D\}\), where \(G\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(D\) is convex polyhedral. Suppose the constraint system is nondegenerate at \(\bar x\in\Gamma\). For \(\bar v\in N_\Gamma(\bar x)\), let \(\bar\lambda\in N_D(G(\bar x))\) be the unique multiplier satisfying \(\nabla G(\bar x)^*\bar\lambda=\bar v\), and set \(K:=T_\Gamma(\bar x)\cap\bar v^\perp\). Then
\[
DN_\Gamma(\bar x,\bar v)(w)=\nabla^2\langle\bar\lambda,G\rangle(\bar x)w+N_K(w).
\]
The right-hand side is empty whenever \(w\notin K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under nondegeneracy, the normal-map derivative equals the Lagrangian curvature term plus the normal cone to the critical cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Nonlinear Constraint Systems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf, but the precise nondegeneracy condition and exact graphical-derivative formula require an authoritative source with a theorem or section locator.

children.top_down_role: Second-order reduction through smooth mappings and structured target sets.

assumptions_latex: \(G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^q\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^q\) is closed.
A second-order normal-cone chain rule holds at \((\bar x,\bar v)\), with a unique multiplier \(\bar\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(DN_\Gamma( ar x, ar v)(w)=
abla^2\langle ar\lambda,Gangle( ar x)w+
abla G( ar x)^*DN_D(G( ar x), ar\lambda)(
abla G( ar x)w)\).

notation.meaning: Graphical derivative of the target normal mapping.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact graphical-derivative reduction under an explicit second-order chain-rule qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Gamma:=G^{-1}(D)\), where \(G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^q\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^q\) is closed. Fix \((\bar x,\bar v)\in\operatorname{gph}N_\Gamma\), and suppose the applicable normal-cone chain rule is exact and yields a unique \(\bar\lambda\in N_D(G(\bar x))\) with \(\nabla G(\bar x)^*\bar\lambda=\bar v\). If its second-order graphical-derivative qualification also holds, then
\[
DN_\Gamma(\bar x,\bar v)(w)=\nabla^2\langle\bar\lambda,G\rangle(\bar x)w+\nabla G(\bar x)^*DN_D(G(\bar x),\bar\lambda)(\nabla G(\bar x)w).
\]
Hence all nonsmooth curvature is transferred to the structured target set \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A qualified smooth-composite system reduces normal-map differentiation to smooth Lagrangian curvature and the target set's normal-map derivative.
knowledge_statements.title: Smooth-Composite Constraint Systems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and reduction theme fit, but the assumed 'applicable' exact chain rule is circular rather than an explicit qualification; a source is needed to determine sufficient hypotheses.

children.title: Second-Order Cone Systems
children.top_down_role: Second-order geometry specialized to second-order cones.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(DN_Q(x,y)(w)=\alpha\mathcal H_xw+N_K(w)\), where \(\mathcal H_x(s,z)=(0,(I-qq^\top)z/t)\).

notation.meaning: Critical cone at the normal pair.
Curvature operator of the smooth nonzero boundary.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-map derivative on the smooth nonzero boundary of one Lorentz cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q:=\{(t,u):t\geq\|u\|\}\), take \(x=(t,u)\in\partial Q\setminus\{0\}\), and put \(q:=u/t\). Every \(y\in N_Q(x)\) has the form \(y=\alpha(-1,q)\) with \(\alpha\geq0\). Define \(K:=T_Q(x)\cap y^\perp\) and the linear curvature operator \(\mathcal H_x(s,z):=(0,(I-qq^\top)z/t)\). Then
\[
DN_Q(x,y)(w)=\alpha\mathcal H_xw+N_K(w).
\]
Thus the second-order-cone normal derivative separates into boundary curvature and a critical-cone normal term; the formula also covers \(\alpha=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a nonzero Lorentz-cone boundary point, the normal derivative splits into explicit boundary curvature and a critical-cone normal.
knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Cone Systems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The boundary-curvature representation fits second-order cone systems, but its sign, scaling, and inclusion of the zero-multiplier case need an authoritative locator.

children.title: Semidefinite Constraint Systems
children.top_down_role: Spectral curvature and normal-map evaluation for positive-semidefinite cones.

assumptions_latex: The columns of \(P_0\) form an orthonormal basis of \(\ker X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T^2_{\mathbb{S}_+^m}(X,W)=\{Z:P_0^\top(Z-2WX^\dagger W)P_0\in T_{\mathbb{S}_+^r}(P_0^\top WP_0)\}\).

notation.meaning: Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of the base matrix.
Orthonormal matrix spanning the kernel of the base matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer second-order tangent geometry of the positive-semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\in\mathbb{S}_+^m\), let \(W\in T_{\mathbb{S}_+^m}(X)\), and let the columns of \(P_0\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times r}\) form an orthonormal basis of \(\ker X\). With \(X^\dagger\) denoting the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse, the outer second-order tangent set satisfies
\[
T^2_{\mathbb{S}_+^m}(X,W)=\left\{Z\in\mathbb{S}^m:P_0^\top(Z-2WX^\dagger W)P_0\in T_{\mathbb{S}_+^r}(P_0^\top WP_0)\right\}.
\]
The correction \(2WX^\dagger W\) is the spectral curvature generated by coupling the nullspace and positive-eigenvalue subspaces of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PSD second-order feasibility is determined on the kernel after subtracting an explicit pseudoinverse-based spectral curvature correction.
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Constraint Systems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The PSD spectral-curvature representation fits the leaf, but the factor two and outer second-order tangent convention require a specific source locator.
