children.title: Eigenvalue-Based Second-Order Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Second-order evaluation organized through eigenvalue-dependent spectral structure.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\frac{d^2}{dt^2}\lambda_i(A+tH)|_{t=0}=2\sum_{j\ne i}\frac{|u_j^\top Hu_i|^2}{\lambda_i(A)-\lambda_j(A)}\).

notation.meaning: Ordered eigenvalues of the symmetric matrix.
Orthonormal eigenvectors of the symmetric matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical simple-eigenvalue second derivative along an affine symmetric-matrix path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A,H\in\mathbb{S}^m\), and suppose \(\lambda_i(A)\) is simple. Choose an orthonormal eigenbasis \(u_1,\ldots,u_m\) satisfying \(Au_j=\lambda_j(A)u_j\). Then the eigenvalue branch through \(\lambda_i(A)\) is twice differentiable along \(A+tH\), with
\[
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\lambda_i(A+tH)\right|_{t=0}=u_i^\top Hu_i,
\qquad
\left.\frac{d^2}{dt^2}\lambda_i(A+tH)\right|_{t=0}=2\sum_{j\ne i}\frac{|u_j^\top Hu_i|^2}{\lambda_i(A)-\lambda_j(A)}.
\]
The denominators encode the spectral-gap dependence of the second-order evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simple eigenvalue's second directional derivative is an explicit spectral-gap-weighted sum of squared cross-eigenspace couplings.
knowledge_statements.title: Eigenvalue-Based Second-Order Evaluation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The simple-eigenvalue formulas are mathematically standard and appropriately classified as a representation, but the record supplies no citation.

children.title: Singular-Value-Based Second-Order Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Second-order evaluation organized through singular-value-dependent spectral structure.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\frac{d^2}{dt^2}\sigma_i(A+tH)|_{t=0}=2\sum_{k\ne i}\frac{|z_k^\top\mathcal B(H)z_i|^2}{\sigma_i(A)-\theta_k}\).

notation.meaning: Symmetric dilation of a rectangular matrix.
Simple positive singular value under evaluation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simple positive singular value evaluated through symmetric dilation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A,H\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), define the symmetric dilation \(\mathcal B(A):=\begin{pmatrix}0&A\\A^\top&0\end{pmatrix}\). Suppose \(\sigma_i(A)>0\) is simple, so it is a simple eigenvalue of \(\mathcal B(A)\). Let \((\theta_k,z_k)\) be an orthonormal eigenbasis of \(\mathcal B(A)\), indexed so that \(\theta_i=\sigma_i(A)\). Then
\[
\left.\frac{d^2}{dt^2}\sigma_i(A+tH)\right|_{t=0}=2\sum_{k\ne i}\frac{|z_k^\top\mathcal B(H)z_i|^2}{\sigma_i(A)-\theta_k}.
\]
This converts singular-value second-order evaluation into the corresponding symmetric eigenvalue calculation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The second derivative of a simple positive singular value is obtained by applying the simple-eigenvalue formula to the symmetric dilation.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Value-Based Second-Order Evaluation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The symmetric-dilation reduction fits the terminal container, but the complete dilation-spectrum indexing and formula need a cited authoritative locator.

children.title: Matrix-Valued Mapping Geometry
children.top_down_role: Second-order geometry associated with structured mappings taking matrix values.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{S}^m\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(K\subset\mathbb{S}^m\) is closed.
A second-order tangent inverse-image qualification holds at \(\bar x\in F^{-1}(K)\) in direction \(w\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T^2_{F^{-1}(K)}(\bar x,w)=\{z:F'(\bar x)z+F''(\bar x)[w,w]\in T^2_K(F(\bar x),F'(\bar x)w)\}\).

notation.meaning: Feasible inverse image of the matrix set.
First derivative of the matrix-valued mapping.
Second derivative evaluated twice in the direction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order tangent chain rule for a smooth matrix-valued inverse image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{S}^m\) be twice continuously differentiable, let \(K\subset\mathbb{S}^m\) be closed, and set \(\Gamma:=F^{-1}(K)\). Fix \(\bar x\in\Gamma\) and \(w\in T_\Gamma(\bar x)\). Under a qualification ensuring exact second-order tangent calculus for this inverse image,
\[
T^2_\Gamma(\bar x,w)=\left\{z\in\mathbb{R}^n:F'(\bar x)z+F''(\bar x)[w,w]\in T^2_K(F(\bar x),F'(\bar x)w)\right\}.
\]
Consequently, matrix-valued constraint curvature consists of the intrinsic second-order geometry of \(K\) combined with the acceleration \(F''(\bar x)[w,w]\) of the mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Qualified second-order feasibility for a matrix-valued constraint is the pullback of target-set second-order geometry plus mapping acceleration.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Valued Mapping Geometry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inverse-image representation fits matrix-valued mapping geometry, but 'a qualification ensuring exact calculus' does not state checkable hypotheses; a source is needed to select the valid theorem version.

children.title: Spectral Multiplicity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Evaluation regimes distinguished by simple, repeated, or changing spectral values.

assumptions_latex: \(\lambda\) is an eigenvalue of \(A\) with eigenspace basis \(U\), and \(V\) spans a selected eigenspace of \(U^\top HU\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The second derivatives in that first-order subcluster are the eigenvalues of \(V^\top U^\top[K+2H(\lambda I-A)^\dagger H]UV\).

notation.meaning: Orthonormal basis matrix for the repeated-eigenvalue eigenspace.
Basis for an eigenspace of the first-order compression.
Moore-Penrose inverse on the complement of the eigenspace.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated symmetric eigenvalues resolved first by compression, then by a second compressed operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A(t)=A+tH+\tfrac12t^2K+o(t^2)\) with symmetric \(A,H,K\), and let \(\lambda\) be an eigenvalue of \(A\) whose eigenspace has orthonormal basis matrix \(U\). The first derivatives of the eigenvalue branches issuing from \(\lambda\) are the eigenvalues of \(U^\top HU\). Fix such a derivative \(\mu\), and let \(V\) span the corresponding eigenspace of \(U^\top HU\). The second derivatives of the branches in this subcluster are the eigenvalues of
\[
V^\top U^\top\left[K+2H(\lambda I-A)^\dagger H\right]UV.
\]
Thus multiplicity requires successive diagonalization within nested active spectral subspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a repeated eigenvalue, first derivatives come from one compression; each tied first-order cluster is resolved by a curvature-corrected second compression.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Multiplicity Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Successive compression is appropriate for spectral multiplicity regimes, but the branch-ordering convention and curvature operator require an authoritative theorem locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order sufficiency yields L2-local quadratic growth for distributed elliptic control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The distributed control problem (4.31)–(4.33) in spatial dimension at most three, with the control integrand specified by (4.109).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose Assumption 4.14 holds for the distributed control problem (4.31)--(4.33), where \dim\Omega=N\leq3. Let \bar u\in U_{ad}\subset L^2(\Omega), with associated state \bar y=G(\bar u) and adjoint state p, satisfy the first-order necessary optimality conditions of Theorem 4.20, and let \psi be of the form (4.109). If (\bar y,\bar u) satisfies the second-order sufficient condition (4.103), then there exist \varepsilon>0 and \sigma>0 such that, for every u\in U_{ad} satisfying \|u-\bar u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\leq\varepsilon, with y=G(u), \[J(y,u)\geq J(\bar y,\bar u)+\sigma\|u-\bar u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2.\] In particular, \bar u is locally optimal in L^2(\Omega).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the specified distributed elliptic control problem in dimension at most three, the stated first- and second-order conditions and the prescribed form of psi imply L2 quadratic growth throughout a sufficiently small L2 neighborhood, hence L2-local optimality.

(\bar y,\bar u,p)\text{ satisfies the first-order necessary optimality conditions of Theorem 4.20.}
(\bar y,\bar u)\text{ satisfies the second-order sufficient condition (4.103).}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-Order Directional Chain Rule for a Convex Composite
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition of a twice continuously differentiable mapping with a lower-semicontinuous convex extended-real function under Robinson's constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G:X\to Y be twice continuously differentiable, let f:Y\to\overline{\mathbb R} be lower semicontinuous and convex, and set y_0:=G(x_0), with f(y_0)\in\mathbb R. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedricity of a Closed Convex Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise and global polyhedricity in a Banach space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K be a closed convex subset of a Banach space Y. The set K is polyhedric at y_0\in K if, for every y^*\in N_K(y_0),\n\[T_K(y_0)\cap\ker y^*=\operatorname{cl}\!\left(R_K(y_0)\cap\ker y^*\right).\]\nIt is polyhedric if it is polyhedric at every y_0\in K.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cone-Induced Lattice Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the continuous lattice order induced by a pointed closed convex cone and records the associated meet and signed-part identities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $K\subset Y$ be a pointed closed convex cone, and let $\preccurlyeq_K$ denote its induced order. The cone $K$ induces a lattice structure on $Y$ when, for every $a,b\in Y$, the least upper bound $a\vee b$ exists and the map $\vee:Y\times Y\to Y$ is continuous. The greatest lower bound $a\wedge b$ satisfies $a\wedge b\preccurlyeq_K a$, $a\wedge b\preccurlyeq_K b$, and $u\preccurlyeq_K a,\ u\preccurlyeq_K b\Rightarrow u\preccurlyeq_K a\wedge b$. Under this lattice structure, $a\wedge b=a+b-(a\vee b)$. With $y_+:=y\vee0$ and $y_-:=y\wedge0$, one has $y=y_-+y_+$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pointed closed convex cone induces a lattice structure when every pair has a least upper bound and the join operation is continuous. The meet is the greatest common lower bound; under this structure it equals the sum minus the join, and every vector decomposes as its meet and join with zero.
assumptions_latex: K\subset Y\text{ is a pointed closed convex cone}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ induces a lattice structure on }Y\text{ when }(\forall a,b\in Y)\ a\vee b\text{ exists and }\vee\text{ is continuous};\ \text{then }a\wedge b=a+b-(a\vee b)\text{ and }y=(y\wedge0)+(y\vee0).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth inverse-image constraint under Robinson's constraint qualification.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tangent Sets of a Finite Union
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite unions of closed subsets of a Banach space; equality holds for the outer first- and second-order tangent sets, while only inclusion is asserted for the corresponding inner sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let S_1,\ldots,S_n\subset X be closed sets in a Banach space X and S:=\bigcup_{k=1}^n S_k. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-Order Necessary and Sufficient Conditions in a Hilbert Space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained smooth optimization under the open-convex-domain and Lipschitz-Hessian assumptions of the preceding estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a Hilbert space, \(U\subset H\) be open and convex, and \(f:U\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable with Lipschitz-continuous Hessian. (a) If \(\widehat u\) is an optimal solution, then \((\operatorname{Hess}f(\widehat u)h,h)\ge0\) for every \(h\in H\). (b) If \(\nabla f(\widehat u)=0\) and there exists \(c>0\) such that \((\operatorname{Hess}f(\widehat u)h,h)\ge c\|h\|^2\) for every \(h\in H\), then \(\widehat u\) is a local minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an optimum, the Hessian is positive semidefinite. Conversely, a stationary point whose Hessian is uniformly positive definite is a local minimum when the Hessian satisfies the stated Lipschitz condition.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a Hilbert space and \(U\subset H\) is open and convex.
\(\operatorname{Hess}f\) satisfies the Lipschitz condition of the preceding Taylor estimate.
For the sufficient condition, \(\nabla f(\widehat u)=0\) and \((\operatorname{Hess}f(\widehat u)h,h)\ge c\|h\|^2\) for all \(h\in H\) and some \(c>0\).

notation.meaning: Second subderivative relative to the zero subgradient.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real local minimum using the lower second subderivative normalized by one-half squared step length.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, and suppose \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer with \(f(\bar x)<+\infty\). Then \(0\in\widehat\partial f(\bar x)\). With the second subderivative defined by
\[
d^2f(\bar x\mid0)(w):=\liminf_{\substack{t\downarrow0\\w'\to w}}\frac{f(\bar x+tw')-f(\bar x)}{\tfrac12t^2},
\]
one has
\[
d^2f(\bar x\mid0)(w)\geq0\qquad\text{for every }w\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
The value \(+\infty\) is permitted, so the condition applies without assuming twice epi-differentiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite local minimizer has zero as a regular subgradient, and its lower second subderivative relative to zero is nonnegative in every direction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric necessity along parabolically feasible arcs for a smooth objective over a closed set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed, let \(f\) be twice continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\in C\), and suppose \(\bar x\) locally minimizes \(f\) over \(C\). If \(w\in T_C(\bar x)\) satisfies \(\langle\nabla f(\bar x),w\rangle=0\), then every \(z\in T_C^2(\bar x,w)\), under the convention \(\bar x+tw+\tfrac12t^2z+o(t^2)\in C\), satisfies
\[
\langle\nabla f(\bar x),z\rangle+\langle w,\nabla^2f(\bar x)w\rangle\geq0.
\]
Thus objective curvature and second-order feasible displacement must be jointly nonnegative along each first-order critical direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Along every critical feasible direction, objective Hessian curvature plus the gradient applied to any second-order feasible displacement must be nonnegative.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is closed, \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\in C\), and \(\bar x\) locally minimizes \(f\) over \(C\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical-cone condition expressed through the second subderivative of the constraint indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed, let \(f\) be twice continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\in C\), and suppose \(\bar x\) locally minimizes \(f\) over \(C\). Assume stationarity with \(\bar v:=-\nabla f(\bar x)\in N_C(\bar x)\), and define \(K:=T_C(\bar x)\cap\bar v^\perp\). Then the second-order necessary condition for the extended-real objective \(f+\delta_C\) is
\[
\langle w,\nabla^2f(\bar x)w\rangle+d^2\delta_C(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)\geq0
\qquad(w\in K).
\]
Directions outside \(K\) do not furnish first-order critical feasible variations and are excluded from this directional test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On every critical direction, smooth objective curvature plus the constraint indicator's second subderivative must be nonnegative.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\le0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) and \(h_j(x)=0\) for \(j=1,\ldots,p\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parabolic second-order necessary and sufficient conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives necessary conditions at a local minimizer and, under parabolic regularity, strict sufficient conditions implying quadratic growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) be proper. If \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer, then
\[
df(\bar x)(w)\ge0\quad\forall w,
\]
and, for every nonzero \(w\) with \(df(\bar x)(w)=0\),
\[
\inf_z d^2f(\bar x)(w\mid z)\ge0.
\]
Conversely, suppose \(f\) is parabolically regular at \(\bar x\) for \(v=0\), \(df(\bar x)(w)\ge0\) for all \(w\), and
\[
\inf_z d^2f(\bar x)(w\mid z)>0
\]
for every nonzero \(w\) with \(df(\bar x)(w)=0\). Then \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer and there exist \(\varepsilon,\delta>0\) such that
\[
f(x)\ge f(\bar x)+\varepsilon\lVert x-\bar x\rVert^2\quad\text{whenever }\lVert x-\bar x\rVert\le\delta.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a local minimizer, every first subderivative is nonnegative, and every nonzero direction with zero first-order growth has nonnegative minimal parabolic second-order growth. Conversely, if the function is parabolically regular for the zero vector, all first subderivatives are nonnegative, and the minimal parabolic second-order growth is strictly positive in every nonzero critical direction, then the point is locally optimal and satisfies a quadratic-growth bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\text{ locally minimizing}\Rightarrow\begin{cases}df(\bar x)(w)\ge0&\forall w,\\\inf_zd^2f(\bar x)(w\mid z)\ge0&\forall w\ne0:\ df(\bar x)(w)=0,\end{cases}\quad\text{and the strict conditions plus parabolic regularity imply quadratic growth.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Quadratic Bound on an Approximating Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The cone family has weak sequential outer-limit containment in the limiting cone as its parameter decreases to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a reflexive Banach space, \(Q:X\to\mathbb R\) an extended Legendre form, \(C\subset X\) a closed convex cone, and \((C_\eta)_{\eta>0}\) cones such that \(\eta_k\downarrow0\), \(h_k\in C_{\eta_k}\), and \(h_k\rightharpoonup\bar h\) imply \(\bar h\in C\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict positivity of an extended Legendre form on a closed convex limiting cone yields a uniform positive quadratic lower bound on one approximating cone, provided weak limits from cones with vanishing parameters lie in the limiting cone.

Q:X\to\mathbb R\text{ is an extended Legendre form}
C\subset X\text{ is a closed convex cone}
\eta_k\downarrow0,\ h_k\in C_{\eta_k},\ h_k\rightharpoonup\bar h\Rightarrow\bar h\in C

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximized-Hessian second-order sufficient condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition in the generalized-Lagrangian framework; the subsequent pointwise condition is explicitly weaker, not equivalent in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a feasible point \(x_0\in\Phi\), the second-order sufficient condition holds when there exist \(\eta>0\) and \(\beta>0\) such that
\[
\sup_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_N^g(x_0)}D_{xx}^2L^g(x_0,\alpha,\lambda)(h,h)\ge \beta\lVert h\rVert^2\qquad\forall h\in C_\eta(x_0).
\]
The left-hand side is called the maximized Hessian of the generalized Lagrangian. This condition implies the weaker condition
\[
\forall h\in C(x_0)\setminus\{0\},\ \exists(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda^g(x_0):\ D_{xx}^2L^g(x_0,\alpha,\lambda)(h,h)>0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The second-order sufficient condition is uniform positive definiteness of the maximized generalized-Lagrangian Hessian on an approximate critical cone. It implies pointwise positive curvature along every nonzero critical direction for a possibly direction-dependent multiplier pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{SOSC}(x_0)\iff\exists\eta,\beta>0\ \forall h\in C_\eta(x_0):\ \sup_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_N^g(x_0)}D_{xx}^2L^g(x_0,\alpha,\lambda)(h,h)\ge\beta\lVert h\rVert^2;\quad \operatorname{SOSC}(x_0)\Rightarrow(3.137).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic-growth tests for generalized polyhedral constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized-Lagrangian and ordinary-Lagrangian Hessian characterizations on the critical cone when the constraint set is generalized polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be generalized polyhedral and let \(x_0\in\Phi\). If there exists \(\beta>0\) such that
\[
\sup_{(\alpha,\lambda)\in\Lambda_N^g(x_0)}D_{xx}^2L^g(x_0,\alpha,\lambda)(h,h)\ge\beta\lVert h\rVert^2\qquad\forall h\in C(x_0),
\]
then quadratic growth holds at \(x_0\). If, additionally, Robinson's constraint qualification holds at \(x_0\), then quadratic growth holds at \(x_0\) if and only if there exists \(\beta>0\) such that
\[
\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda(x_0)}D_{xx}^2L(x_0,\lambda)(h,h)\ge\beta\lVert h\rVert^2\qquad\forall h\in C(x_0).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For generalized polyhedral constraints, uniform positivity of the maximized generalized-Lagrangian Hessian on the critical cone is sufficient for quadratic growth. Under Robinson's constraint qualification, quadratic growth is equivalent to the corresponding ordinary-Lagrangian multiplier test.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{RCQ}(x_0)\text{ is required only for the necessary-and-sufficient characterization}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Near-optimal feasible sequences approach through approximate critical cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the feasible set \(\Phi\), critical cone \(C(x_0)\), and approximate critical cones \(C_\eta(x_0)\) from the surrounding second-order framework.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{x_n\}\subset\Phi\) be feasible, let \(x_n\to x_0\), and suppose \(f(x_n)\le f(x_0)+o(\|x_n-x_0\|)\). Then, for every \(\eta>0\), \(x_n-x_0\in C_\eta(x_0)\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). If, additionally, \(X\) is finite dimensional, then there exist \(h\in C(x_0)\setminus\{0\}\), a subsequence \(x_{n(k)}\), and numbers \(t_k>0\) with \(t_k\downarrow0\) such that \(x_{n(k)}=x_0+t_kh+o(t_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any feasible sequence converging to x0 with objective value no worse than f(x0) up to a term negligible relative to its distance from x0 eventually has displacement in every approximate critical cone. In finite dimensions, a subsequence admits a first-order expansion along a nonzero critical direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\eta>0,\ \exists N\ \forall n\ge N:\ x_n-x_0\in C_\eta(x_0);\quad \dim X<\infty\Rightarrow\exists h\in C(x_0)\setminus\{0\},\ x_{n(k)}=x_0+t_kh+o(t_k),\ t_k\downarrow0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parabolic Second-Order Necessary and Growth Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality and quadratic-growth tests on the critical cone under first-order stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_0\) be feasible and satisfy \(f_-^{\downarrow}(x_0,\cdot)\ge0\). Then:

(i) If \(x_0\) is a local minimizer, then
\[
\inf_{w\in X}f_-^{\downarrow\downarrow}(x_0;h,w)\ge0\qquad\forall h\in C(x_0).
\]

(ii) If, in addition, \(X\) is finite-dimensional and \(f\) is parabolically regular at \(x_0\) for \(\alpha=0\), then the second-order growth condition holds at \(x_0\) if and only if
\[
\inf_{w\in X}f_-^{\downarrow\downarrow}(x_0;h,w)>0\qquad\forall h\in C(x_0)\setminus\{0\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under first-order stationarity, local optimality forces nonnegativity of the infimal parabolic second-order derivative in every critical direction. In finite dimensions, with parabolic regularity for the zero covector, second-order growth is equivalent to strict positivity in every nonzero critical direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left[x_0\text{ local minimizer}\Rightarrow \inf_{w\in X}f_-^{\downarrow\downarrow}(x_0;h,w)\ge0\ \forall h\in C(x_0)\right],\quad \left[\text{second-order growth}\iff \inf_{w\in X}f_-^{\downarrow\downarrow}(x_0;h,w)>0\ \forall h\in C(x_0)\setminus\{0\}\right]

d^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(\bar x)d>0\qquad\text{for every }d\ne0,

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \((\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\) satisfies the KKT conditions and LICQ holds. If
\[
d^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^{2}L(\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)d>0
\qquad\text{for all }d\in K(\bar x)\setminus\{0\},
\]
then there exist \(c,r>0\) such that every feasible \(x\) with \(\lVert x-\bar x\rVert<r\) satisfies
\[
f(x)\ge f(\bar x)+\frac c2\lVert x-\bar x\rVert^2.
\]
Consequently, \(\bar x\) is a strict, isolated local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive Lagrangian curvature on every nonzero critical direction implies feasible quadratic growth and isolated local minimality under LICQ.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume there is \(\alpha>0\) such that
\[
d^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^{2}L(\bar x,\lambda,\mu)d
\ge \alpha\lVert d\rVert^2
\]
for every \(d\in K(\bar x)\) and every \((\lambda,\mu)\in\Lambda(\bar x)\). Then the second-order sufficient condition is independent of multiplier selection. Under MFCQ, this uniform curvature bound implies that there exist \(c,r>0\) for which
\[
f(x)\ge f(\bar x)+\frac c2\lVert x-\bar x\rVert^2
\]
for all feasible \(x\) with \(\lVert x-\bar x\rVert<r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If all admissible multipliers give uniformly positive Lagrangian curvature on the critical cone, the point satisfies feasible quadratic growth.

children.title: Parabolic Second-Order Sufficiency
children.top_down_role: Sufficiency families using parabolic regularity and second-order feasible geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) is closed.
\(\Omega\) is parabolically derivable at \(\bar x\) in every critical direction.
The displayed curvature bound holds uniformly over unit critical directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The uniform parabolic curvature bound implies quadratic growth of \(f\) on \(\Omega\) at \(\bar x\).

notation.meaning: Critical directions \(d\in T_\Omega(\bar x)\) satisfying \(\nabla f(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}d=0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parabolically derivable finite-dimensional feasible sets with a uniform second-order growth margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(\nabla f(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}d\ge0\) for all \(d\in T_\Omega(\bar x)\), and assume that some \(\alpha>0\) satisfies
\[
\inf_{w\in T^2_\Omega(\bar x;d)}
\left(\nabla f(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}w+d^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(\bar x)d\right)
\ge\alpha
\]
for every \(d\in K_f(\bar x)\) with \(\lVert d\rVert=1\). Under parabolic derivability and the regularity ensuring realization of these second-order tangents, there exist \(c,r>0\) such that
\[
f(x)\ge f(\bar x)+\frac c2\lVert x-\bar x\rVert^2
\]
for all \(x\in\Omega\cap B_r(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly positive objective curvature over all unit critical directions and feasible parabolic corrections yields constrained quadratic growth.
knowledge_statements.title: Parabolic Second-Order Sufficiency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement fits the parabolic sufficiency leaf, but the phrase concerning regularity ensuring realization does not state a checkable hypothesis. A source is required to determine the precise parabolic derivability or regularity assumptions, the tangent-set convention, and whether the displayed uniform bound suffices for quadratic growth.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linearized State Equation and Tau-Critical Cone for Parabolic Boundary Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the linearized state generated by a boundary-control direction and the pointwise restrictions defining the tau-critical cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a reference state $\bar y$, the linearized state $z$ associated with a boundary-control direction $v$ satisfies
\[
z_t-\Delta z+d_y(x,t,\bar y)z=0\quad\text{in }Q,
\qquad \partial_\nu z+b_y(x,t,\bar y)z=v\quad\text{on }\Sigma,
\qquad z(0)=0\quad\text{in }\Omega.
\]
For $\tau>0$,
\[
C_\tau(\bar u)=\left\{v\in L^\infty(\Sigma):
\begin{array}{l}
v(x,t)=0\quad\text{on }A_\tau(\bar u),\\
v(x,t)\geq0\quad\text{when }\bar u(x,t)=u_a\text{ outside }A_\tau(\bar u),\\
v(x,t)\leq0\quad\text{when }\bar u(x,t)=u_b\text{ outside }A_\tau(\bar u)
\end{array}\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A boundary-control direction generates a linearized parabolic state with homogeneous initial data. The tau-critical cone contains the essentially bounded directions that vanish on the tau-active set, are nonnegative at the lower control bound outside that set, and are nonpositive at the upper control bound outside that set. The displayed definition imposes no additional sign restriction at points not covered by these cases.
assumptions_latex: \bar y\text{ and }\bar u\text{ are the reference state and control, respectively}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_t-\Delta z+d_y(x,t,\bar y)z=0,\quad \partial_\nu z+b_y(x,t,\bar y)z=v,\quad z(0)=0,\quad v\in C_\tau(\bar u)\iff v\text{ satisfies the stated regional restrictions}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Growth from a Parabolic Second-Order Sufficient Condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient condition for local quadratic growth in semilinear parabolic boundary control, localized in the control's $L^\infty$ norm and measured quadratically in its $L^2$ norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose Assumption 5.6 holds, and let $(\bar y,\bar u)$ be feasible for the optimal boundary-control problem and satisfy the first-order necessary optimality conditions. If there exist $\delta>0$ and $\tau>0$ such that the definiteness condition (5.49) holds, then there exist $\varepsilon>0$ and $\sigma>0$ such that, for every $u\in U_{ad}$ with associated state $y$ and
\[
\|u-\bar u\|_{L^\infty(\Sigma)}\leq\varepsilon,
\]
one has
\[
J(y,u)\geq J(\bar y,\bar u)+\sigma\|u-\bar u\|_{L^2(\Sigma)}^2.
\]
Consequently, $\bar u$ is locally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assume the referenced regularity hypothesis, feasibility, the first-order necessary conditions, and the stated second-order definiteness condition for some positive delta and tau. Then every admissible control sufficiently close to the reference control in the L-infinity norm satisfies a positive L2 quadratic-growth bound. Thus the reference control is locally optimal in the indicated L-infinity neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: (\bar y,\bar u)\text{ is feasible and satisfies the first-order necessary optimality conditions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\varepsilon>0\;\exists\sigma>0\;\forall u\in U_{ad}:\ \|u-\bar u\|_{L^\infty(\Sigma)}\leq\varepsilon\Longrightarrow J(y,u)\geq J(\bar y,\bar u)+\sigma\|u-\bar u\|_{L^2(\Sigma)}^2;\quad \bar u\text{ is locally optimal}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic growth at one fixed reference point for an extended-real objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The function \(F\) has pointwise quadratic growth at \(\bar x\) if there exist constants \(c>0\) and \(r>0\) such that
\[
F(x)\ge F(\bar x)+\frac c2\lVert x-\bar x\rVert^2
\qquad\text{whenever }\lVert x-\bar x\rVert<r.
\]
For an extended-real function, points outside \(\operatorname{dom}F\) satisfy the inequality automatically. The constants may depend on the designated point \(\bar x\); no uniformity over nearby minimizers or perturbations is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective has pointwise quadratic growth when it rises at least quadratically away from one designated minimizer within a neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Quadratic Growth

children.title: Uniform Quadratic Growth
children.top_down_role: Growth uniform under nearby base points or perturbations.

assumptions_latex: \(F_p:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is a family indexed by \(p\) near \(\bar p\).
For each relevant \(p\), a reference point \(x_p\) satisfies \(F_p(x_p)<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One common pair \((c,r)\) supplies quadratic growth for every nearby parameter and its associated reference point.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A parameterized formulation distinguishing uniform growth from growth only at one base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The family \(\{F_p\}\) has uniform quadratic growth around \((\bar p,\bar x)\) along reference points \(x_p\) if there exist \(c,r,\rho>0\) such that, whenever \(\lVert p-\bar p\rVert<\rho\),
\[
F_p(x)\ge F_p(x_p)+\frac c2\lVert x-x_p\rVert^2
\qquad\text{for all }x\in B_r(x_p).
\]
The constants \(c\) and \(r\) are independent of \(p\). Taking a singleton parameter set recovers pointwise quadratic growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform quadratic growth uses the same positive growth modulus and neighborhood radius for all nearby parameters and associated minimizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Quadratic Growth

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed parameter-uniform definition is compatible with the leaf's role, but the parameter normed space, the relation between \(x_p\) and \((\bar p,\bar x)\), and the admissible reference-point selection are not specified. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Second-Order Growth under Smooth Parameterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform quadratic growth around every nearby stationary point of a parameterized constrained problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let x_0 be stationary for the reference problem. Uniform second-order growth at x_0 relative to a C^2-smooth parameterization (f(x,u),G(x,u)) means that there exist c>0 and neighborhoods \mathcal V_X of x_0 and \mathcal V_U of u_0 such that, for every u\in\mathcal V_U and every stationary point \bar x(u)\in\mathcal V_X of P_u, f(x,u)\geq f(\bar x(u),u)+c\|x-\bar x(u)\|^2 for all x\in\mathcal V_X satisfying G(x,u)\in K. The unqualified uniform second-order growth condition holds when this property holds for every C^2-smooth parameterization. For the canonical parameterization, the condition becomes f(x)-\langle\delta_1,x-\bar x\rangle\geq f(\bar x)+c\|x-\bar x\|^2 for every x\in\mathcal V_X\cap G^{-1}(K-\delta_2).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform second-order growth requires a positive quadratic-growth constant that applies uniformly to nearby parameters, nearby stationary points, and nearby feasible points. Without qualification, the requirement is imposed for every twice-smooth parameterization.
assumptions_latex: x_0\text{ is stationary for the reference problem}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists c>0,\mathcal V_X,\mathcal V_U:\ \forall u\in\mathcal V_U,\ \forall\bar x(u)\in\mathcal V_X\text{ stationary},\ \forall x\in\mathcal V_X\text{ with }G(x,u)\in K,\quad f(x,u)\geq f(\bar x(u),u)+c\|x-\bar x(u)\|^2.

children.top_down_role: Isolated minimizers supported by local growth.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and finite at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) is a strong local minimizer exactly when it satisfies a local quadratic-growth inequality with positive modulus.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong local minimality in the quadratic-growth sense used in second-order variational analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A point \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}F\) is a strong local minimizer of \(F\) if there exist \(c>0\) and \(r>0\) such that
\[
F(x)\ge F(\bar x)+\frac c2\lVert x-\bar x\rVert^2
\qquad\text{for every }x\in B_r(\bar x).
\]
This inequality implies that \(\bar x\) is the unique minimizer of \(F\) in a possibly smaller neighborhood. Thus strong local minimality is stronger than strict local minimality without a prescribed growth rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strong local minimizer is supported by a positive quadratic lower bound and is therefore locally isolated.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Local Minimizers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quadratic-growth definition of a strong local minimizer is standard in second-order variational analysis and fits the leaf, but terminology varies across sources. No inspectable citation is provided to establish the intended convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent characterizations of strong local minimizers in polyhedral quadratic programming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes strong local minimality for a quadratic objective over a polyhedron using critical-cone curvature and isolation properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x with Q=Q^\top, let P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\ge b\}, and let \bar x\in P. The following are equivalent: (i) \bar x is stationary and v^\top Qv>0 for every nonzero v\in\mathcal C(\bar x;q;P); (ii) \bar x is stationary, Q is copositive on \mathcal C(\bar x;q;P), and [v\in\mathcal C(\bar x;q;P),\ Qv\in\mathcal C(\bar x;q;P)^*,\ v^\top Qv=0]\Rightarrow v=0; (iii) \bar x is a local minimizer and an isolated stationary point; (iv) \bar x is an isolated local minimizer; (v) \bar x is a strict local minimizer; and (vi) \bar x is a strong local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a quadratic program over a polyhedron, strong local minimality is equivalent to strict positivity of the quadratic form on every nonzero critical direction. It is also equivalent to the stated dual-cone nondegeneracy condition and to several isolation and strict-minimality properties.
assumptions_latex: Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n},\quad Q=Q^\top,\quad c\in\mathbb R^n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&[\bar x\text{ stationary and }v^\top Qv>0\ \forall v\in\mathcal C(\bar x;q;P)\setminus\{0\}]\\&\iff[\bar x\text{ stationary},\ Q\text{ copositive on }\mathcal C,\ (v\in\mathcal C,\ Qv\in\mathcal C^*,\ v^\top Qv=0)\Rightarrow v=0]\\&\iff[\bar x\text{ is a local minimizer and an isolated stationary point}]\\&\iff[\bar x\text{ is an isolated local minimizer}]\iff[\bar x\text{ is a strict local minimizer}]\iff[\bar x\text{ is a strong local minimizer}].\end{aligned}

notation.meaning: Second epi-derivative of \(F\) at \(\bar x\) relative to the subgradient \(0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional prox-regular, subdifferentially continuous, twice epi-differentiable objectives at a stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the stated regularity, the following are equivalent: there exist \(c,r>0\) such that
\[
F(x)\ge F(\bar x)+\frac c2\lVert x-\bar x\rVert^2
\quad\text{for }x\in B_r(\bar x),
\]
and there exists \(\alpha>0\) such that
\[
d_e^2F(\bar x\mid0)(d)\ge\alpha\lVert d\rVert^2
\quad\text{for every }d\in\mathbb R^n.
\]
Thus, within this regularity regime, strong local minimality is characterized by uniform positive second-order epi-curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For regular twice epi-differentiable objectives, local quadratic growth is equivalent to uniformly positive second-order epi-curvature in every direction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order conditions for unconstrained optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the second subderivative of a proper extended-real-valued function at a stationary point relative to the zero subgradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) be proper. If \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of \(f\), then \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)\) and \(\mathrm d^2f(\bar x\mid 0)(w)\ge 0\) for every \(w\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Conversely, if \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)\) and \(\mathrm d^2f(\bar x\mid 0)(w)>0\) for every \(w\ne0\), then \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer. Moreover, these strict second-order conditions are equivalent to the existence of \(\varepsilon,\delta>0\) such that \(f(x)\ge f(\bar x)+\varepsilon\lVert x-\bar x\rVert^2\) whenever \(\lVert x-\bar x\rVert\le\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper extended-real-valued function, every local minimizer is stationary and has a nonnegative second subderivative in every direction. Stationarity together with strict positivity of the second subderivative in every nonzero direction is sufficient for local optimality and is equivalent to a local quadratic-growth bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\text{ locally minimizes }f\Rightarrow\bigl[0\in\partial f(\bar x),\ \mathrm d^2f(\bar x\mid0)(w)\ge0\ \forall w\bigr],\quad \bigl[0\in\partial f(\bar x),\ \mathrm d^2f(\bar x\mid0)(w)>0\ \forall w\ne0\bigr]\Longleftrightarrow\bigl[\exists\varepsilon,\delta>0:\ f(x)\ge f(\bar x)+\varepsilon\lVert x-\bar x\rVert^2\ \text{if }\lVert x-\bar x\rVert\le\delta\bigr].

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\le0\) and \(h_j(x)=0\). If \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer and LICQ holds, then its KKT multiplier satisfies
\[
d^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^{2}L(\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)d\ge0
\quad\text{for every }d\in K(\bar x).
\]
Conversely, if the KKT conditions hold and the displayed inequality is strict for every nonzero \(d\in K(\bar x)\), then \(\bar x\) satisfies feasible quadratic growth and is a strong local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under LICQ, nonlinear-program local optimality requires nonnegative Lagrangian curvature on the critical cone, while strict positivity there ensures quadratic growth.

notation.meaning: Critical cone for the conic constraint system.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth conic programming expressed through the indicator's second subderivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(G(x)\in K\). Let \(\lambda\in N_K(G(\bar x))\) satisfy \(\nabla f(\bar x)+G'(\bar x)^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\). Under a valid second-order chain rule, local minimality requires
\[
d^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^{2}L(\bar x,\lambda)d
+d^2\delta_K(G(\bar x)\mid\lambda)(G'(\bar x)d)\ge0
\]
for critical directions \(d\in\mathcal C(\bar x,\lambda)\). A uniform strict lower bound by \(\alpha\lVert d\rVert^2\) for all nonzero critical directions is sufficient for quadratic growth. The indicator term records nonpolyhedral cone curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conic second-order tests add the cone indicator's second subderivative to Lagrangian curvature; strict positivity gives quadratic growth under chain-rule regularity.
knowledge_statements.title: Conic Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The indicator second-subderivative formula belongs in the conic-programming leaf, but necessity is asserted for an arbitrarily selected stationary multiplier. With nonunique multipliers, a directional selection, maximization, or stronger qualification may be required. assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is twice continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
\(g:\mathbb R^m\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and twice epi-differentiable at \(F(\bar x)\) for each relevant multiplier.
A second-order composite chain rule holds at \(\bar x\), and \(0\in\partial(g\circ F)(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_e^2(g\circ F)(\bar x\mid0)(w)>0\) for every \(w\ne0\) is a strict second-order sufficient condition.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f=g\circ F\) and define \(\Lambda( ar x)=\{y\in\partial g(F( ar x)):
abla F( ar x)^*y=0\}\). Under the stated chain-rule qualification, the second epi-derivative admits the multiplier reduction \[d_e^2 f( ar x\mid0)(w)=\max_{y\in\Lambda( ar x)}\left\{\langle y,
abla^2F( ar x)[w,w]angle+d_e^2g(F( ar x)\mid y)(
abla F( ar x)w)ight\}.\] Consequently, nonnegativity of this expression in every direction is second-order necessary for a local minimum, while strict positivity for every nonzero direction is a strict second-order sufficient condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact composite chain rule reduces second-order optimality to multiplier-indexed curvature. Nonnegativity is necessary, and positivity in every nonzero direction is sufficient for strict local minimality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The sufficient conclusion is retained by its source theorem reference because the packet does not state Theorem 5.3.3.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be polyhedral, let \(\bar z=(\bar x,\bar y)\) be stationary for the MPEC, suppose \(\bar z\) is strongly regular, and suppose \(f,F\in C^2\) near \(\bar z\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The variational inequality solution set is \[S=\{x\in C:\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\ge0\ \text{for every }y\in C\}=\{x:0\in F(x)+N_C(x)\}.\] At \(\bar x\in S\), its critical cone is \(K=T_C(\bar x)\cap F(\bar x)^\perp\). The associated linearized solution set is \[L=\{w:0\in\nabla F(\bar x)w+DN_C(\bar x\mid-F(\bar x))(w)\}.\] Every tangent direction to \(S\) belongs to \(L\); equality holds when the generalized equation is graphically derivable and its residual mapping satisfies an appropriate local error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variational inequality is a normal-cone generalized equation. Its tangent directions satisfy the graphical-derivative linearization, with equality under graphical derivability and a local error bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Map Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean normal-map reformulation of a convex-set variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(P_C\) be its Euclidean projector, and define \[F_C(z)=F(P_Cz)+z-P_Cz.\] The zeros of the normal map and the solutions of the variational inequality correspond by \[F_C(z)=0,\quad x=P_Cz\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad 0\in F(x)+N_C(x),\quad z=x-F(x).\] Consequently, \[\{x\in\mathbb R^n:0\in F(x)+N_C(x)\}=\{P_Cz:z\in\mathbb R^n,\ F_C(z)=0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The zeros of the normal map correspond exactly to variational-inequality solutions: a zero z gives x=P_Cz, while a solution x gives z=x−F(x).
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_C(z)=0\) with \(x=P_Cz\) if and only if \(0\in F(x)+N_C(x)\) with \(z=x-F(x)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \widehat z(u)=(\widehat x(u),\widehat\lambda(u)) satisfy the approximate optimality conditions with \delta=O(\lVert u-u_0\rVert), and suppose \widehat x(u)\to x_0 as u\to u_0. knowledge_statements.title: Strong Metric-Regularity Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prox-regular subgradient mappings at a stationary local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be prox-regular and subdifferentially continuous at \((\bar x,0)\), where \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer and \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)\). Then the following properties are equivalent: \(\bar x\) is a tilt-stable local minimizer; \(\partial f\) is strongly metrically regular at \((\bar x,0)\); and there exists \(c>0\) such that \[\langle z,w\rangle\ge c\|w\|^2\quad\text{for every }w\in\mathbb R^n\text{ and every }z\in\partial^2f(\bar x\mid0)(w).\] Strong metric regularity means that a localization of \((\partial f)^{-1}\) around \((0,\bar x)\) is single-valued and Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a prox-regular stationary local minimizer, strong metric regularity of the subgradient mapping, tilt stability, and uniform positive definiteness of the limiting generalized Hessian are equivalent.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is prox-regular and subdifferentially continuous at \((\bar x,0)\).
\(\bar x\) is a local minimizer and \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Tilt stability of \(\bar x\), strong metric regularity of \(\partial f\) at \((\bar x,0)\), and uniform positive definiteness of \(\partial^2f(\bar x\mid0)\) are equivalent.

knowledge_statements.title: Isolated-Calmness Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graphical-derivative test for isolated calmness of a subgradient solution map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=(\partial f)^{-1}\), and suppose that \(\operatorname{gph}\partial f\) is locally closed at \((\bar x,\bar v)\). The map \(S\) is isolated calm at \((\bar v,\bar x)\) if and only if \[0\in D(\partial f)(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad w=0.\] Equivalently, \[DS(\bar v\mid\bar x)(0)=\{0\}.\] Isolated calmness means that there are neighborhoods \(V\) of \(\bar v\) and \(U\) of \(\bar x\), and \(\kappa>0\), such that \[S(v)\cap U\subset \bar x+\kappa\|v-\bar v\|\mathbb B\quad\text{for every }v\in V.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the subgradient graph is locally closed, its inverse is isolated calm exactly when the homogeneous graphical linearization has no nonzero primal solution direction.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
\(\operatorname{gph}\partial f\) is locally closed at \((\bar x,\bar v)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\partial f)^{-1}\) is isolated calm at \((\bar v,\bar x)\) if and only if \(0\in D(\partial f)(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)\Rightarrow w=0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=(\partial f)^{-1}\). The Aubin property of \(S\) at \((\bar v,\bar x)\) means that some neighborhoods and \(\kappa>0\) satisfy \[S(v_1)\cap U\subset S(v_2)+\kappa\|v_1-v_2\|\mathbb B\] for all nearby \(v_1,v_2\). The coderivative criterion yields \[S\text{ has the Aubin property at }(\bar v,\bar x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\partial^2f(\bar x\mid\bar v)(w)\Rightarrow w=0.\] This is the second-order injectivity test for Lipschitz-like solution behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inverse subgradient map is Lipschitz-like exactly when zero belongs to the generalized Hessian in no nonzero direction.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\le0\). Let \((\bar x,\bar\lambda)\) satisfy the KKT conditions and LICQ, and let \(K(\bar x,\bar\lambda)\) be the corresponding critical cone. If there exists \(c>0\) such that \[\langle w,\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar\lambda)w\rangle\ge c\|w\|^2\quad\text{for every }w\in K(\bar x,\bar\lambda),\] then \(\bar x\) is a tilt-stable local minimizer of the constrained problem. The localized minimizer under small linear objective perturbations is therefore unique and Lipschitz continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under LICQ, uniform positive curvature of the Lagrangian on the critical cone guarantees tilt stability and Lipschitz dependence of the local constrained minimizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Unconstrained Full Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lipschitz full stability under simultaneous tilt and finite-dimensional parameter perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\), \(P=\mathbb{R}^s\), and \(f:X\times P\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\). For \(\gamma>0\), define \[M_\gamma(v,p):=\mathop{\rm argmin}_{x\in B_\gamma(\bar x)}\{f(x,p)-\langle v,x\rangle\},\qquad m_\gamma(v,p):=\inf_{x\in B_\gamma(\bar x)}\{f(x,p)-\langle v,x\rangle\}.\] The minimizer \(\bar x\) is fully stable at \((\bar v,\bar p)\) if some \(\gamma>0\) and neighborhoods of \(\bar v\) and \(\bar p\) make \(M_\gamma\) single-valued and Lipschitz, with \(M_\gamma(\bar v,\bar p)=\bar x\), and make \(m_\gamma\) Lipschitz on the same product neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local minimizer is fully stable when small finite-dimensional tilt and parameter changes produce a unique nearby minimizer and locally Lipschitz minimizer and value mappings.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\), \(P=\mathbb{R}^s\), and \(f:X\times P\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) is proper and lower semicontinuous near \((\bar x,\bar p)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The localized minimizer and value mappings are single-valued Lipschitz near \((\bar v,\bar p)\).

children.title: Full Stability in Nonlinear Programming
children.top_down_role: Multiplier-sensitive full stability for smooth constraint systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Full Stability in Nonlinear Programming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programs with equality and inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(p\in\mathbb{R}^s\), \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^s\to\mathbb{R}^q\), and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^s\to\mathbb{R}^m\). Consider minimizing \(\varphi(x,p)-\langle v,x\rangle\) subject to \(h(x,p)=0\) and \(g(x,p)\leq0\). Suppose \((\bar x,\bar p)\) is feasible and stationary at tilt \(\bar v\), LICQ holds there, and \(\bar\lambda\) is the resulting unique KKT multiplier. Let \(K(\bar x,\bar p,\bar\lambda)\) be the associated critical cone. If \[\langle d,\nabla_{xx}^2L(\bar x,\bar p,\bar\lambda)d\rangle>0\quad\text{for every }d\in K(\bar x,\bar p,\bar\lambda)\setminus\{0\},\] then the localized primal-multiplier KKT solution mapping in \((v,p)\) is single-valued and Lipschitz. Consequently, \(\bar x\) is a fully stable local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear program, LICQ and positive Lagrangian curvature on every nonzero critical direction yield a locally unique Lipschitz primal-multiplier solution and full stability.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi\), \(h\), and \(g\) are \(C^2\) near \((\bar x,\bar p)\), with \(h\) equality-valued in \(\mathbb{R}^q\) and \(g\) inequality-valued in \(\mathbb{R}^m\).
\((\bar x,\bar p)\) is a feasible KKT point at tilt \(\bar v\).
LICQ holds at \((\bar x,\bar p)\), giving the unique multiplier \(\bar\lambda\).
The strong second-order sufficient condition holds on the critical cone \(K(\bar x,\bar p,\bar\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The localized primal-multiplier solution is single-valued Lipschitz, and \(\bar x\) is a fully stable local minimizer.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar v\in\partial_x f(\bar x,\bar p)\). Under the stated qualification, the composite second subderivative is obtained from the smooth second-order terms and the second subderivative of \(\theta\). A sufficient full-stability condition is the existence of \(\kappa>0\) such that \[d^2f(\bar x,\bar p\mid\bar v)(w)\geq\kappa\lVert w\rVert^2\quad\text{for every }w\in K(\bar x,\bar v).\] Together with prox-regularity and subdifferential continuity, this condition yields a single-valued Lipschitz localization of the tilt-parameterized minimizer mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A qualified composite objective is fully stable when its reduced second subderivative is uniformly positive on all critical directions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order tangent set of the nonnegative W^{1,\infty} cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The active sets \Delta(f), \Delta_1(f,\eta) and correction \zeta_{f,\eta} arise from the associated minimum-function perturbation problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let K=W_+^{1,\infty}(\Phi), f\in K, and \eta\in T_K(f). Assume \Delta(f) and \Delta_1(f,\eta) are nonempty and finite and that, at every x_0\in\Delta(f), f and \eta are Hadamard directionally differentiable, f is twice directionally differentiable and second-order epiregular in every critical direction, the underlying feasible set is second-order regular in every critical direction, and second-order growth holds. Then K is second-order regular at f in direction \eta and
\[
T_K^2(f,\eta)=\{u\in W^{1,\infty}(\Phi):u(x)+\zeta_{f,\eta}(x)\ge0\ \text{for every }x\in\Delta_1(f,\eta)\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonnegative W^{1,infinity} function whose zero and first-order active sets are finite, the stated local second-order hypotheses imply second-order regularity of the positivity cone. Its second-order tangent set consists exactly of perturbations satisfying a corrected nonnegativity inequality at every first-order active zero.
assumptions_latex: \forall x_0\in\Delta(f),\text{ the directional differentiability, second-order epiregularity, set regularity, and second-order growth assumptions hold}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ is second-order regular at }f\text{ in direction }\eta,\quad T_K^2(f,\eta)=\{u\in W^{1,\infty}(\Phi):u(x)+\zeta_{f,\eta}(x)\ge0\ \forall x\in\Delta_1(f,\eta)\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order derivative of a min-function with finitely many minimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The correction \zeta_{f,\eta}(x) is the second-order local value coefficient determined by critical directions and second-order tangent sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \mathcal S(f) is finite and, at every x\in\mathcal S(f), f and \eta are Hadamard directionally differentiable, f is twice directionally differentiable and second-order epiregular in every critical direction, the feasible set is second-order regular in every critical direction, and the corresponding unperturbed problem satisfies second-order growth. Then the min-function v is second-order directionally differentiable and second-order regular at f in direction \eta, and for every \varrho,
\[
v''(f;\eta,\varrho)=\min_{x\in\mathcal S_1(f,\eta)}\{\varrho(x)+\zeta_{f,\eta}(x)\},\qquad \mathcal S_1(f,\eta)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathcal S(f)}\eta(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the minimizer set is finite and the local differentiability, second-order regularity, epiregularity, and growth hypotheses hold at every minimizer, then the minimum functional is second-order directionally differentiable and regular. Its second derivative is the minimum of the perturbation plus the local second-order correction over first-order active minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \forall x\in\mathcal S(f),\ f,\eta\text{ are Hadamard directionally differentiable at }x
\forall x\in\mathcal S(f),\ f\text{ is twice directionally differentiable and second-order epiregular in every }h\in C(x)
\forall x\in\mathcal S(f),\ \Phi\text{ is second-order regular in every }h\in C(x)
\forall x\in\mathcal S(f),\text{ the corresponding second-order growth condition holds}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v\text{ is second-order directionally differentiable and second-order regular at }f\text{ in direction }\eta,\quad v''(f;\eta,\varrho)=\min_{x\in\mathcal S_1(f,\eta)}\{\varrho(x)+\zeta_{f,\eta}(x)\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inner and Outer Second-Order Tangents to \(C_+(\Omega)\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representations, a necessary outer-tangent bound, and the epiconvergence criterion for equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega\) be a compact metric space, \(K=C_+(\Omega)\), \(x\in K\), and \(h\in T_K(x)\). Define
\[
\tau_{x,h}:=-\operatorname{e\!-
liminf}_{t\downarrow0}\frac{x+th}{t^2/2},\qquad
\tau_{x,h}^*:=-\operatorname{e\!-
limsup}_{t\downarrow0}\frac{x+th}{t^2/2}.
\]
Then
\[
T_K^{i,2}(x,h)=\{z\in C(\Omega):z(\omega)\geq\tau_{x,h}(\omega)\ \forall\omega\in\Omega\},
\]
and this set is nonempty iff \(\tau_{x,h}(\omega)<+\infty\) for all \(\omega\). Every \(z\in T_K^2(x,h)\) satisfies \(z(\omega)\geq\tau_{x,h}^*(\omega)\) for all \(\omega\). Finally,
\[
T_K^{i,2}(x,h)=T_K^2(x,h)
\]
if and only if \(f_t=(x+th)/(t^2/2)\) epiconverges as \(t\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inner second-order tangent set to the positive cone is the set of continuous majorants of an epigraphical-liminf threshold and is nonempty exactly when that threshold is finite everywhere. Outer second-order tangents majorize the corresponding epigraphical-limsup threshold. The inner and outer sets coincide exactly when the scaled functions epiconverge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_K^{i,2}(x,h)=\{z\in C(\Omega):z\geq\tau_{x,h}\},\quad z\in T_K^2(x,h)\Rightarrow z\geq\tau_{x,h}^*,\quad T_K^{i,2}(x,h)=T_K^2(x,h)\iff f_t\xrightarrow{e}f

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local derivative and coderivative structure near a prox-regular stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R} be prox-bounded, let 0\in\partial f(\widetilde x), and suppose f is prox-regular at \widetilde x for 0. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Connected-Approach Criterion for Second-Order Tangent Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient boundary condition for equality of inner and outer second-order tangent sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega\) be a compact metric space, \(K=C_+(\Omega)\), \(x\in K\), and \(h\in T_K(x)\). Suppose that for every \(\omega\in\operatorname{bdr}\Delta(x)\) with \(h(\omega)=0\) and \(\theta(\omega)>0\), there is a connected set \(\Gamma_\omega\subset\Omega\) such that \(\omega\) is a limit point of \(\Gamma_\omega\), \(x(\omega')>0\) for all \(\omega'\in\Gamma_\omega\), and
\[
\limsup_{\substack{\omega'\to\omega\\x(\omega')>0}}
\frac{([-h(\omega')]_+)^2}{2x(\omega')}
=
\liminf_{\substack{\omega'\to\omega\\\omega'\in\Gamma_\omega}}
\frac{([-h(\omega')]_+)^2}{2x(\omega')}.
\]
Then \(\tau_{x,h}=\tau_{x,h}^*\), and consequently
\[
T_K^{i,2}(x,h)=T_K^2(x,h).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If each relevant boundary point can be approached through a connected positive region along which the lower limiting growth ratio attains the unrestricted upper limiting ratio, then the lower and upper second-order thresholds coincide, so the inner and outer second-order tangent sets are equal.
assumptions_latex: \forall\omega\in\operatorname{bdr}\Delta(x)\text{ with }h(\omega)=0,\ \theta(\omega)>0,\ \exists\Gamma_\omega\text{ satisfying the stated connectedness, positivity, limit-point, and limit-equality conditions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \tau_{x,h}=\tau_{x,h}^*\quad\text{and}\quad T_K^{i,2}(x,h)=T_K^2(x,h)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Formula for the Positive-Cone Second-Order Threshold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Piecewise evaluation of the inner second-order tangent threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega\) be a compact metric space, \(K=C_+(\Omega)\), \(x\in K\), and \(h\in T_K(x)\). The threshold \(\tau_{x,h}\) is
\[
\tau_{x,h}(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
0,&\omega\in\operatorname{int}\Delta(x)\text{ and }h(\omega)=0,\\
\theta(\omega),&\omega\in\operatorname{bdr}\Delta(x)\text{ and }h(\omega)=0,\\
-\infty,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]
where
\[
\theta(\omega):=\limsup_{\substack{\omega'\to\omega\\x(\omega')>0}}
\frac{([-h(\omega')]_+)^2}{2x(\omega')}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The second-order tangent threshold is zero at interior points of the active set where the direction vanishes, equals a boundary growth ratio at boundary active points where the direction vanishes, and is minus infinity otherwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \tau_{x,h}(\omega)=\begin{cases}0&\omega\in\operatorname{int}\Delta(x),\ h(\omega)=0,\\\theta(\omega)&\omega\in\operatorname{bdr}\Delta(x),\ h(\omega)=0,\\-\infty&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\quad \theta(\omega)=\limsup_{\omega'\to\omega,\,x(\omega')>0}\frac{([-h(\omega')]_+)^2}{2x(\omega')}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order directional derivative of the min-function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Here v(u)=min_{x\in\Phi}u(x), while \vartheta and \mathcal S_1 are the associated second-order correction and first-order active-minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \Phi be a compact metric space and v:C(\Phi)\to\mathbb R be the min-function. For every u,\eta,\varrho\in C(\Phi),
\[
v_-''(u;\eta,\varrho)=\begin{cases}\inf_{x\in\mathcal S_1(u,\eta)}\{\varrho(x)-\vartheta(x)\},&\mathcal S_1(u,\eta)\ne\varnothing,\\0,&\mathcal S_1(u,\eta)=\varnothing.\end{cases}
\]
Moreover, if for every x_0\in\mathcal S_1(u,\eta) there is a continuous path \bar x:[0,1]\to\Phi with \bar x(0)=x_0, u(\bar x(t))>v(u) for t>0, and
\[
\limsup_{\substack{x\to x_0\\u(x)>v(u)}}\frac{([v'(u,\eta)-\eta(x)]_+)^2}{2[u(x)-v(u)]}=\liminf_{t\downarrow0}\frac{([v'(u,\eta)-\eta(\bar x(t))]_+)^2}{2[u(\bar x(t))-v(u)]},
\]
then v_-''(u;\eta,\cdot)=v_+''(u;\eta,\cdot), so v is twice directionally differentiable at u in direction \eta.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lower second directional derivative of the minimum functional is the infimum of the corrected second-order perturbation over the first-order active minimizers, or zero when that set is empty. If each active minimizer admits a continuous escaping path along which the defining limsup correction is attained, the lower and upper second directional derivatives coincide.
assumptions_latex: \forall x_0\in\mathcal S_1(u,\eta)\text{, the stated continuous path and limit-attainment condition hold for the differentiability conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_-''(u;\eta,\varrho)=\begin{cases}\inf_{x\in\mathcal S_1(u,\eta)}(\varrho(x)-\vartheta(x)),&\mathcal S_1(u,\eta)\ne\varnothing,\\0,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\quad\text{and under the path condition }v_-''(u;\eta,\cdot)=v_+''(u;\eta,\cdot).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent criteria for differentiability of a strongly stable parametric VI solution map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes Fréchet differentiability through critical directions, unique AVIs, and linearized multiplier systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\) solve \(\operatorname{VI}(K(p^*),F(\cdot,p^*))\) and satisfy MFCQ, CRCQ, and SCOC, and let \(x_{\mathcal N}\) be the resulting implicit \(\mathrm{PC}^1\) solution function. The following are equivalent: (a) \(x_{\mathcal N}\) is Fréchet differentiable at \(p^*\); (b) for every \(dp\in\mathbb R^n\), \(x'_{\mathcal N}(p^*;dp)\in\mathcal E(x^*,p^*;dp)\); (c) for every \(dp\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\lambda\in\mathcal M^e(x^*,p^*)\), that derivative is the unique solution of the associated critical AVI; (d) for every such \(dp,\lambda\) and every maximal \(\mathcal J\in\mathcal B(x^*,p^*)\) containing \(\operatorname{supp}(\lambda)\), the derivative together with some \(d\lambda_{\mathcal J}\) uniquely solves the stated stationarity and active-constraint linearization equations; (e) there exist one such \(\lambda\) and maximal \(\mathcal J\) for which this unique linear-system characterization holds for every \(dp\in\mathbb R^p\). Whenever these conditions hold, \(\mathcal M^c(x^*,p^*;dp)=\mathcal M(x^*,p^*)\) for every \(dp\in\mathbb R^p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the piecewise continuously differentiable solution map furnished by MFCQ, CRCQ, and strong coherent orientation, Fréchet differentiability is equivalent to several directional conditions: membership in the distinguished direction set, unique solvability of every relevant critical AVI, and unique solvability of the corresponding primal-multiplier linearized equations. Under these conditions every multiplier is directionally critical in every parameter direction.
assumptions_latex: x_{\mathcal N}\text{ is the implicit }\mathrm{PC}^1\text{ parametric-VI solution function.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (a)\iff(b)\iff(c)\iff(d)\iff(e),\qquad \text{and each implies }\mathcal M^c(x^*,p^*;dp)=\mathcal M(x^*,p^*)\ \forall dp\in\mathbb R^p.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity is relative to the specified embedding \iota; the active sets and correction arise from the associated minimum-function perturbation problem.

Assume \Delta(f) and \Delta_1(f,\eta) are nonempty and finite and that, at every x_0\in\Delta(f), f and \eta are Hadamard directionally differentiable, f is twice directionally differentiable and second-order epiregular in every critical direction, the underlying feasible set is second-order regular in every critical direction, and second-order growth holds. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sequential Inner Second-Order Tangent Set of the Positive Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequence-dependent representation and nonemptiness criterion in \(C(\Omega)_+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega\) be a compact metric space, \(K=C_+(\Omega)\), \(x\in K\), \(h\in T_K(x)\), and \(\sigma=\{t_n\}\in\Sigma\). Define
\[
\tau_{x,h}^{\sigma}:=-\operatorname{e\!-
liminf}_{n\to\infty}\frac{x+t_nh}{t_n^2/2}.
\]
Then
\[
T_K^{i,2,\sigma}(x,h)=\{z\in C(\Omega):z(\omega)\geq\tau_{x,h}^{\sigma}(\omega)\ \forall\omega\in\Omega\}.
\]
Moreover, this set is nonempty if and only if \(\tau_{x,h}^{\sigma}(\omega)<+\infty\) for every \(\omega\in\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the cone of nonnegative continuous functions, the sequential inner second-order tangent set consists exactly of continuous majorants of the negative epigraphical lower limit of the scaled functions. It is nonempty exactly when that threshold is finite everywhere.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order value expansion and sensitivity of nearly optimal solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The notation C(x), T_\Phi^2(x,h), \varepsilon_t, and the perturbed problems P_{u_t} is inherited from the underlying perturbation framework.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let x_0 be the unique solution of (P), and let \bar x(t) be an o(t^2)-optimal solution of (P_{u_t}). Suppose f and \eta are Hadamard directionally differentiable at x_0; f is twice directionally differentiable at x_0 and second-order epiregular there in every h\in C(x_0); \Phi is second-order regular at x_0 in every h\in C(x_0); and (P) satisfies second-order growth at x_0. Define
\[
\zeta_{f,\eta}(x):=\inf_{h\in C(x)}\left\{2\eta'(x,h)+\inf_{w\in T_\Phi^2(x,h)}f''(x;h,w)\right\}.
\]
Then, for t\ge0,
\[
v(t)=v(0)+t\eta(x_0)+\varepsilon_t(x_0)+\tfrac12t^2\zeta_{f,\eta}(x_0)+o(t^2).
\]
Furthermore, \bar x(t) is Lipschitz stable at x_0, and every limit point of t^{-1}(\bar x(t)-x_0) as t\downarrow0 solves
\[
\min_{h\in C(x_0)}\left\{\eta'(x_0,h)+\tfrac12\inf_{w\in T_\Phi^2(x_0,h)}f''(x_0;h,w)\right\}.
\]
If this auxiliary problem has the unique solution \bar h, then \bar x(t)=x_0+t\bar h+o(t).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under directional differentiability, second-order epiregularity and set regularity, uniqueness, and second-order growth, the perturbed optimal value has a second-order expansion. Nearly optimal solutions are Lipschitz stable, their normalized first-order displacements solve a second-order auxiliary problem, and uniqueness of that solution yields a first-order expansion of the optimizer.
assumptions_latex: x_0\text{ is the unique optimal solution of }(P)
f,\eta\text{ are Hadamard directionally differentiable at }x_0
f\text{ is twice directionally differentiable at }x_0
f\text{ is second-order epiregular at }x_0\text{ for every }h\in C(x_0)
\Phi\text{ is second-order regular at }x_0\text{ for every }h\in C(x_0)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v(t)=v(0)+t\eta(x_0)+\varepsilon_t(x_0)+\tfrac12t^2\zeta_{f,\eta}(x_0)+o(t^2),\quad \bar x(t)\text{ is Lipschitz stable, and if the auxiliary minimizer }\bar h\text{ is unique, }\bar x(t)=x_0+t\bar h+o(t).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz Robustness under Right-Hand-Side and Linear-Operator Perturbations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A strong-regularity consequence for affine perturbations of a linearized generalized equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let z_0 be a strongly regular solution of the abstract generalized equation. There exist neighborhoods \mathcal V_Z of z_0, \mathcal V_W of 0\in W, and \mathcal V_L of D\varphi(z_0)\in\mathcal L(Z,W) such that, for every (\delta,A)\in\mathcal V_W\times\mathcal V_L, the generalized equation
\delta\in\varphi(z_0)+A(z-z_0)+N(z)
has a unique solution z(\delta,A)\in\mathcal V_Z. Moreover, for some \kappa>0,
\|z(\delta',A')-z(\delta,A)\|\leq\kappa(\|\delta'-\delta\|+\|A'-A\|)
for all admissible perturbation pairs.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-Order Directional Derivatives of the Max Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper and lower second-order derivative formulas on \(C(\Phi)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi\) be a compact metric space and let \(\bar v:C(\Phi)\to\mathbb R\) be the max function. For all \(u,\eta,\varrho\in C(\Phi)\), define
\[
\bar u(\cdot)=\bar v(u)-u(\cdot),\qquad
\bar\eta(\cdot)=\bar v'(u;\eta)-\eta(\cdot).
\]
Then
\[
\bar v_{+}''(u;\eta,\varrho)=\sup_{x\in\Phi}\{\varrho(x)+\tau_{\bar u,\bar\eta}(x)\},
\]
and
\[
\bar v_{-}''(u;\eta,\varrho)=\inf_{\sigma\in\Sigma}\sup_{x\in\Phi}\{\varrho(x)+\tau_{\bar u,\bar\eta}^{\sigma}(x)\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the max functional on continuous functions over a compact metric space, the upper second-order directional derivative is the supremum of the second-order perturbation plus the inner tangent threshold. The lower derivative is the infimum over admissible vanishing sequences of the corresponding suprema with sequence-dependent thresholds.
assumptions_latex: \bar v:C(\Phi)\to\mathbb R\text{ is the max function}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar v_{+}''(u;\eta,\varrho)=\sup_{x\in\Phi}(\varrho(x)+\tau_{\bar u,\bar\eta}(x)),\qquad \bar v_{-}''(u;\eta,\varrho)=\inf_{\sigma\in\Sigma}\sup_{x\in\Phi}(\varrho(x)+\tau_{\bar u,\bar\eta}^{\sigma}(x))

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Surjectivity and Kernel Coercivity Characterize KKT-System Isomorphism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence for a self-adjoint operator that is nonnegative on the kernel of a Banach-space constraint operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X$ and $Y$ be Banach spaces, $H\in\mathcal L(X,X^*)$ be self-adjoint, and $A\in\mathcal L(X,Y)$. Assume $\langle Hx,x\rangle\ge 0$ for every $x\in\ker A$. Then the following are equivalent: (i) for every $(x^*,y)\in X^*\times Y$, there exists a unique $(\bar x,\bar y^*)\in X\times Y^*$ satisfying $H\bar x+A^*\bar y^*=x^*$ and $A\bar x=y$; (ii) $A$ is onto and there exists $\alpha>0$ such that $\langle Hx,x\rangle\ge\alpha\|x\|^2$ for every $x\in\ker A$.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subsmoothness and Subdifferential Formula for a Parametric Value Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper-C1 regularity, almost-everywhere strict differentiability, and derivative formulas in terms of parameter gradients at minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
p(u)=\inf_x f(x,u),\qquad P(u)=\operatorname*{argmin}_x f(x,u),
\]
where f:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m\to\overline{\mathbb{R}} is proper, lsc, and level-bounded in x locally uniformly in u. Let \bar u\in\operatorname{dom}p. Suppose open sets W\in\mathcal N(\bar u) and V\supset P(\bar u) exist such that \nabla_u f(x,u) exists on V\times W and both f and \nabla_u f are continuous there. Then p is upper-\mathcal C^1 on W and strictly differentiable on a set D\subset W whose complement is negligible. With
\[
Y(u)=\{\nabla_u f(x,u)\mid x\in P(u)\},
\]
one has u\in D iff Y(u) is a singleton. Moreover,
\[
dp(\bar u)(z)=\min_{y\in\bar\nabla p(\bar u)}\langle y,z\rangle=\min_{y\in Y(\bar u)}\langle y,z\rangle,
\]
\[
\partial p(\bar u)=\bar\nabla p(\bar u)\subset Y(\bar u),\qquad \operatorname{con}\bar\nabla p(\bar u)=\operatorname{con}Y(\bar u).
\]
In particular, if \bar u\in D, then \partial p(\bar u)=Y(\bar u).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper lower-semicontinuous objective that is locally uniformly level-bounded in the decision variable and continuously differentiable in the parameter near the reference minimizers, the value function is upper-C1 and strictly differentiable except on a negligible set. Differentiability occurs exactly when all minimizers yield the same parameter gradient, and its directional derivative and limiting subdifferential are characterized by those gradients.
assumptions_latex: f(x,u)\text{ is level-bounded in }x\text{ locally uniformly in }u
W\in\mathcal N(\bar u),\quad V\supset P(\bar u)\text{ are open}
f\text{ and }\nabla_u f\text{ are continuous on }V\times W
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\text{ is upper-}\mathcal C^1\text{ on }W;\ W\setminus D\text{ is negligible};\ u\in D\iff Y(u)\text{ is a singleton};\ dp(\bar u)(z)=\min_{y\in Y(\bar u)}\langle y,z\rangle;\ \partial p(\bar u)=\bar\nabla p(\bar u)\subset Y(\bar u),\ \operatorname{con}\bar\nabla p(\bar u)=\operatorname{con}Y(\bar u).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong approximation in the solution variable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform first-order approximation with respect to the solution variable for mappings between Banach spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:X\times Y\to Z\) be a mapping between Banach spaces. A mapping \(h:Y\to Z\) strongly approximates \(f\) in \(y\) at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) if \(h(\bar y)=f(\bar x,\bar y)\) and, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exist neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(V\) of \(\bar y\) such that
\[\|[f(x,y_1)-h(y_1)]-[f(x,y_2)-h(y_2)]\|\le\varepsilon\|y_1-y_2\|\]
for all \(x\in U\) and \(y_1,y_2\in V\). Equivalently, \(g(x,y):=f(x,y)-h(y)\) is strictly differentiable in \(y\) at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) with \(\nabla_yg(\bar x,\bar y)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strong approximation matches f at the reference point and leaves a residual f−h whose local Lipschitz slope in the y-variable can be made arbitrarily small, uniformly for nearby x. Equivalently, that residual is strictly differentiable in y with zero derivative at the reference point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: h\text{ strongly approximates }f\text{ in }y\text{ at }(\bar x,\bar y)\iff h(\bar y)=f(\bar x,\bar y)\text{ and the stated uniform residual estimate holds.}

children.top_down_role: Full-stability criteria for parameterized generalized equations.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized-Equation Full Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lipschitz full stability for finite-dimensional parameterized generalized equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\), \(P=\mathbb{R}^s\), and \(F:X\times P\rightrightarrows X\). Define \[S(v,p):=\{x\in X\mid 0\in F(x,p)+v\}.\] The reference solution \(\bar x\) is fully stable at \((\bar v,\bar p)\) if neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(W\) of \((\bar v,\bar p)\) exist such that \(S_U(v,p):=S(v,p)\cap U\) is a singleton for every \((v,p)\in W\), \(S_U(\bar v,\bar p)=\{\bar x\}\), and the resulting selection is Lipschitz on \(W\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-dimensional generalized-equation solution is fully stable when every nearby perturbation has one nearby solution and that solution varies Lipschitz-continuously.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\), \(P=\mathbb{R}^s\), and \(F:X\times P\rightrightarrows X\) has locally closed graph near \(((\bar x,\bar p),-\bar v)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Full stability means that the perturbed generalized equation has a unique nearby solution depending Lipschitz-continuously on \((v,p)\).
